To: Board of Directors, Meridian Foods Corporation
From: Denise Okafor, Chief Financial Officer
Date: March 14, 2024
Re: Acquisition of Prairie Grain Mills and Executive Transition

Dear Board Members,

I am writing to confirm that Meridian Foods Corporation has completed its acquisition of Prairie Grain Mills, headquartered in Wichita, Kansas. The deal, valued at 42 million dollars, closed on March 12, 2024, following approval from regulators in the United States. Meridian will absorb Prairie Grain Mills as a wholly owned subsidiary, retaining its 210 employees and its flagship facility on Route 54.

In related news, effective April 1, 2024, Thomas Reyes will step down as Chief Operating Officer of Meridian Foods Corporation to pursue an opportunity with Cascade Logistics Group in Portland, Oregon. Mr. Reyes has served in this role since 2018 and led the integration of our Ohio distribution center. The Board will meet on March 22, 2024, at our headquarters in Chicago, Illinois, to formally elect Sandra Whitfield as his successor.

Separately, I want to note that Meridian's wire transfer of 42 million dollars to Prairie Grain Mills' former owner, Harold Bennett, was processed by First Union Bank on March 12, 2024, finalizing the transaction.

We anticipate that this acquisition will strengthen our position against competitors such as Golden Harvest Industries, particularly in the Midwest grain-processing sector.

Please direct any questions to my office before the next board meeting.

Sincerely,
Denise Okafor
Chief Financial Officer
Meridian Foods Corporation

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., June 4, 2024 -- Arcadia Biosciences Inc. announced today that it has acquired NovaCell Therapeutics Ltd. for approximately $340 million in cash, expanding its footprint in regenerative medicine. The transaction, finalized on June 3, 2024, was approved by both companies' boards and is expected to close in the third quarter of 2024.

Under the agreement, Arcadia Biosciences will pay NovaCell shareholders $28.50 per share, a premium of 22 percent over the company's closing price on May 30, 2024. NovaCell, headquartered in Oxford, United Kingdom, specializes in stem-cell therapies for degenerative eye disease, including its lead product, RetinoCure.

"This acquisition strengthens our pipeline and accelerates our entry into ophthalmology," said Dr. Miriam Fasano, Chief Executive Officer of Arcadia Biosciences, at a press briefing held in Cambridge. "NovaCell's team, led by Dr. Anthony Reyes, has built something extraordinary over the past eight years."

Dr. Reyes, who founded NovaCell in 2016 in Oxford, will join Arcadia Biosciences as Senior Vice President of Research, effective July 1, 2024. He will report directly to Dr. Fasano.

Arcadia Biosciences, listed on the Nasdaq under ticker ARCB, employs roughly 1,200 people across facilities in Cambridge, San Diego, and Basel, Switzerland. The company reported revenue of $612 million in fiscal year 2023.

Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners called the deal a strategic move against competitor Genovax Pharmaceuticals, which has aggressively expanded its own eye-disease portfolio since 2022.

The merger remains subject to customary regulatory approval, including clearance from the U.K. Competition and Markets Authority.

CAMBRIDGE, MA, March 4, 2024 - Halden Biosciences Inc. announced today that it has acquired Verrix Diagnostics Ltd., a clinical-stage diagnostics company based in Dublin, Ireland, for $340 million in cash and stock. The acquisition, which closed on March 1, 2024, expands Halden's portfolio into early detection tools for pancreatic cancer.

Under the terms of the agreement, Halden Biosciences will pay Verrix Diagnostics shareholders $340 million, with Dr. Fiona Marsh, Verrix's founder and Chief Executive Officer, remaining on board as Senior Vice President of Diagnostics. Dr. Marsh founded Verrix Diagnostics in 2016 and led the company through three rounds of venture funding totaling $85 million.

"This acquisition strengthens our diagnostics pipeline and accelerates our mission to bring earlier cancer detection to patients worldwide," said Raymond Achebe, Chief Executive Officer of Halden Biosciences, speaking at a press briefing in Boston on March 4, 2024.

Halden Biosciences, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs approximately 1,200 people and reported revenue of $612 million in fiscal year 2023. The company's shares trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker HLDB. Verrix Diagnostics, founded in Dublin in 2016, employs 140 scientists and engineers.

As part of the transition, Verrix will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Halden Biosciences, retaining its Dublin research facility. The deal is expected to be finalized pending regulatory review by the European Commission, with full integration anticipated by September 2024.

For more information, contact Halden Biosciences Investor Relations at (617) 555-0198 or visit www.haldenbio.com.

MANCHESTER, England — October 14, 2023. Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice on Saturday as Villa defeated Everton 3-1 at Villa Park in front of 41,822 fans, moving Unai Emery's side into third place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute, converting a low cross from midfielder John McGinn, before doubling his tally just after halftime with a curling finish from 18 yards. Everton captain Seamus Coleman pulled one back in the 68th minute, heading in from a corner kick, but a late strike from substitute Leon Bailey in the 85th minute sealed the win for the home side. Emery, speaking to reporters after the match, praised his squad's resilience, saying the team had "shown real character against a tough Everton side." Everton manager Sean Dyche admitted his team's defending was "far too loose in the final third" and acknowledged that Villa deserved the three points. The result lifted Aston Villa to 19 points from eight matches, while Everton dropped to 16th place with just seven points. Villa will next face Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on October 21, while Everton travel to Newcastle United on the same weekend. Sunday's fixtures also saw Manchester City defeat Brighton 2-0 at the Etihad Stadium, with goals from Erling Haaland and Phil Foden extending Pep Guardiola's unbeaten run to eleven matches this season.

Nadia Reyes

Trellis Capital Partners
Chicago, Illinois

MADRID, October 14, 2023 - Carlos Ibarra scored twice as Atletico Levante defeated Real Sabadell 3-1 at Estadio Municipal on Saturday, extending their unbeaten run to eight matches in the Segunda Division. Ibarra, a 24-year-old forward, opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a header from a corner kick before doubling his tally just before halftime. Sabadell midfielder Diego Ferrante pulled one back in the 63rd minute, but substitute Mateo Guzman sealed the win with a curling strike in the 88th minute. Head coach Ana Beltran praised her squad's discipline after the match, saying the team had "grown up a lot" since losing to Deportivo Cuenca in September. The victory moved Atletico Levante to second place in the standings, four points behind leaders CD Zaragoza. Club president Jorge Villaverde announced after the game that the team had agreed a sponsorship deal worth 2 million euros with Iberia Motors, set to begin in January 2024. Villaverde also confirmed that striker Pablo Nunez, sidelined since August with a knee injury, is expected to return to training next week. Atletico Levante will next travel to Zaragoza on October 21 to face the league leaders at La Romareda, a fixture that could decide the early direction of the title race. Roughly 8,500 fans attended Saturday's match, one of the highest attendances of the season at the 12,000-capacity stadium.

CHICAGO, June 4 -- Meridian Foods Corporation announced today that it has acquired Prairie Grain Snacks LLC, a Des Moines-based maker of organic crackers, for $42 million in cash. The deal, finalized on June 3, is expected to close fully by July 15.

Under the agreement, Meridian will retain Prairie Grain Snacks' 210 employees at its Des Moines production facility and will keep the Prairie Grain Snacks brand intact. Meridian Foods Corporation, headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, is a subsidiary of Halbrook Consumer Holdings and produces snack foods sold across North America.

"This acquisition strengthens our position in the fast-growing organic snacks category," said Denise Warfield, Chief Executive Officer of Meridian Foods Corporation. "Prairie Grain Snacks has built a loyal customer base over the past decade, and we intend to invest an additional $8 million in their facility over the next two years."

Martin Okafor, founder of Prairie Grain Snacks LLC, will join Meridian as Senior Vice President of Organic Products effective July 15, reporting directly to Warfield. Okafor founded the company in Ames, Iowa in 2011 before relocating operations to Des Moines in 2015.

Analysts at Torrance Capital Partners noted the transaction values Prairie Grain Snacks at roughly 3.5 times its annual revenue of $12 million. Meridian's shares rose 4 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement.

Meridian Foods Corporation will host a conference call on June 10 at 9:00 a.m. Central Time to discuss the transaction with investors.

Fjallraven Sweden today began shipping the Kaipak 28 Backpack, a rugged all-weather pack designed for hikers navigating the trails of Sarek National Park. Priced at $189.99 and available in Deep Forest Green and Basalt Grey, the Kaipak 28 features a G-1000 Eco fabric shell, a padded 15-inch laptop sleeve, and a lifetime warranty backed by the company's Ornskoldsvik repair facility. The listing went live on October 14, 2024, through the retailer's flagship store in Portland, Oregon, and on Amazon.

According to product manager Elin Bergstrom, the Kaipak 28 was developed over 18 months in collaboration with Swedish alpine guide Mattias Holm, who tested three prototypes during a 2023 expedition across Kebnekaise. "We wanted something a weekend backpacker in Colorado or a researcher in the Arctic could rely on equally," Bergstrom said in a statement released from the company's Stockholm office.

Each unit ships with a detachable rain cover, two aluminum stays, and a 2-liter hydration bladder compartment. The bag weighs 1.4 kilograms and holds up to 28 liters, roughly 15 percent more capacity than the previous Kaipak 22 model. Customers who order before November 1, 2024 will receive a free set of Fjallraven trekking poles, a $45 value.

Early reviewers on the outdoor forum TrailSpace gave the pack 4.6 out of 5 stars, praising its durability but noting the price is steep compared to competitor Osprey's Atmos AG 65. The Kaipak 28 is currently in stock, with over 3,000 units already sold since launch.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Press Statement - 14 March 2024

The Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure today announced a $420 million investment plan to upgrade the Port of Halden and surrounding rail links over the next three years. Minister Elena Vasquez confirmed the funding during a press briefing held in Oslo, alongside Port Authority Director Magnus Reinholt.

"This initiative will create approximately 1,200 jobs and reduce shipping delays by an estimated 30 percent," Minister Vasquez said. The plan follows a February 2024 feasibility study conducted by Nordic Infrastructure Partners, which identified aging rail infrastructure as the primary bottleneck affecting freight movement between Halden and Gothenburg.

Construction will begin on 1 June 2024, with the first phase focused on expanding the container terminal at Halden. The Ministry has signed a $180 million contract with Baltic Rail Construction AS to complete the rail upgrades by December 2026. Baltic Rail Construction AS, headquartered in Bergen, was selected following a competitive tender process that also included bids from Skandia Engineering Group.

Minister Vasquez will present the full implementation timeline to the Norwegian Parliament on 22 March 2024. Officials from the European Investment Bank, which is co-financing 25 percent of the project, are expected to attend the session. The Ministry emphasized that the upgrade aligns with the national goal of cutting transport-related carbon emissions by 40 percent before 2030.

This statement was issued by the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure on behalf of the Government of Norway.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. HG-24-118873

On March 11, 2024, Judge Patricia Alvarado sentenced Marcus Whitfield, 41, to 63 months in state prison after a jury in Oakland convicted him of embezzlement from his former employer, Lindqvist Freight Systems Inc., a logistics company headquartered in Fremont, California. Prosecutor Daniel Osei of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office had charged Whitfield in September 2023 with grand theft and falsifying business records, alleging that between January 2021 and June 2022 he diverted approximately $840,000 from company accounts into a shell entity called Coastal Ridge Holdings LLC.

During the trial, which began on February 5, 2024, Whitfield's attorney, Renee Castellano, argued that the missing funds reflected accounting errors rather than criminal intent. The jury rejected that defense after two weeks of testimony, returning a guilty verdict on February 20, 2024. Judge Alvarado also ordered restitution of $840,000 payable to Lindqvist Freight Systems Inc. within five years.

Company founder Erik Lindqvist, who started the firm in 1998, said in a statement that the ruling "restores some measure of justice to our employees." Whitfield, who worked as the company's chief financial officer from 2015 until his termination in July 2022, is expected to begin serving his sentence at Santa Rita Jail before transfer to a state facility. His attorney said an appeal will be filed with the California Court of Appeal within 60 days.

BOSTON, MA -- September 12, 2023 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tepavastin, an experimental chemical compound designed to inhibit interleukin-6 signaling in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. The study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, enrolled 214 participants across three sites, including Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston and Northwestern Memorial Hospital in Chicago, between January 2022 and March 2023. Patients receiving 150 milligrams of tepavastin twice daily showed a 47 percent reduction in joint inflammation markers compared to 12 percent in the placebo group after 24 weeks. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings on September 12, 2023 at the American College of Rheumatology conference held in Atlanta, Georgia. "These results suggest tepavastin could offer a meaningful alternative for patients who do not respond to methotrexate," she said during the presentation. The trial was funded by a $8.5 million grant from the National Institutes of Health and conducted in partnership with Vantera Therapeutics, a biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Vantera Therapeutics was founded in 2015 by Dr. Marcus Chen, who currently serves as Chief Scientific Officer. The company plans to begin Phase 3 trials in early 2024, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Approximately 1.3 million adults in the United States are diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Side effects observed during the trial included mild headache and nausea, reported by 9 percent of participants, with no serious adverse events recorded.

Director Karen Wexley said the funding, approved by the Federal Highway Administration, will address structural fatigue identified in a 2023 inspection report. Work is scheduled to begin on March 4, 2024, and is expected to conclude by November 2025. During construction, two of the bridge's six lanes will remain closed to traffic, and detours will route commercial vehicles through the Combs-Hehl Bridge. Governor Michael DeWine, speaking at a press conference in Columbus, praised the agreement between ODOT and the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, calling it "a model of interstate cooperation." The project will be carried out by contractor Kokosing Construction Company, which was awarded the bid last week after a competitive review process. Approximately 140 workers are expected to be employed on site at peak construction. Local officials, including Cincinnati Mayor Aftab Pureval, noted that the bridge carries roughly 172,000 vehicles daily and is a critical corridor for freight moving along Interstate 75. The Department also confirmed that a $6.5 million federal grant, separate from the primary allocation, will fund safety improvements to nearby Route 8. Public comment sessions will be held on January 18 and January 25 at the Duke Energy Convention Center for residents seeking further information about traffic impacts.

SUPERIOR COURT OF FULTON COUNTY, GEORGIA
Case No. 24-CR-1187

On March 11, 2024, Judge Marcia Holloway sentenced Devon Aldrich, 37, to 8 years in state prison after a jury in Atlanta convicted him of armed robbery and aggravated assault stemming from an incident at First Peachtree Bank on October 4, 2023. Prosecutor Renée Castillo of the Fulton County District Attorney's Office argued that Aldrich entered the branch on Peachtree Street armed with a handgun and struck teller Marcus Whitfield, causing a fractured jaw, when Whitfield hesitated to open the vault. Whitfield was transported to Grady Memorial Hospital by ambulance shortly after the attack and was treated for his injuries.

Aldrich was arrested by Atlanta Police Department officers on October 6, 2023, two days after the robbery, following a tip that led investigators to his apartment in East Point. He was formally charged on October 19, 2023, with armed robbery, aggravated assault, and possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony.

During the trial, which began February 20, 2024, defense attorney Paul Ngata contended that Aldrich acted under duress, but the jury, under Judge Holloway's supervision, rejected the argument after two days of deliberation. First Peachtree Bank confirmed that $42,000 was taken during the robbery, though $31,500 was later recovered from a storage unit in Decatur.

The sentence includes 8 years of incarceration followed by 5 years of supervised probation. Aldrich's attorney has indicated plans to appeal the verdict to the Georgia Court of Appeals within 30 days.

Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low finish from inside the box, then added a second in the 58th minute after a swift counterattack led by midfielder John McGinn. Everton pulled one back through striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 71st minute, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win for Villa with a strike in stoppage time. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his team's resilience after the match, saying the club is "building something special" ahead of a Europa Conference League fixture against Legia Warsaw on October 19. Everton manager Sean Dyche said his side's defending was "unacceptable" and admitted the club, currently 17th in the standings, must improve quickly to avoid a relegation battle. CHICAGO, March 14 -- Deere & Company announced Thursday it has acquired Precision AgriTech Inc., a privately held sensor and software maker based in Ames, Iowa, for approximately $740 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by the end of the second quarter, will bring Precision AgriTech's soil-analysis platform under Deere's growing digital agriculture division. John May, Deere's Chief Executive Officer, said the acquisition would help farmers cut fertilizer costs by up to 18 percent within three years. "This is about giving growers real-time data they can trust," May told reporters during a briefing at Deere's headquarters in Moline, Illinois. Precision AgriTech's founder, Rachel Nunn, will join Deere as Vice President of Digital Solutions starting April 1, according to a company statement. Nunn started the firm in 2016 with two former University of Iowa researchers and grew it to 210 employees before the sale. Shares of Deere rose 3.2 percent to $412.55 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of rival Caterpillar Inc. slipped slightly amid renewed speculation about consolidation in the farm-equipment sector. Analysts at Morningstar noted the purchase price represents roughly 9 times Precision AgriTech's projected 2024 revenue of $82 million. Deere financed the transaction using existing cash reserves and a new $300 million credit facility arranged by JPMorgan Chase & Co. The company expects the deal to add modestly to earnings per share in fiscal 2025.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SANTA CLARA COUNTY, CALIFORNIA

Case No. 24-CV-118902

On March 6, 2024, Judge Elaine Torres of the Santa Clara County Superior Court presided over the sentencing hearing of defendant Marcus Whitfield, 41, former financial controller at Denholm Robotics Inc., a robotics manufacturer headquartered in San Jose, California. Prosecutor Angela Ruiz of the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office charged Whitfield with embezzlement and wire fraud on November 14, 2023, alleging he diverted $2.3 million from Denholm Robotics Inc. between January 2021 and August 2023 into a shell account held at Pacific Crest Bank.

During the trial hearing held on January 9, 2024, at the Santa Clara County Courthouse, defense attorney Robert Kim argued that Whitfield acted under duress from his supervisor, though the court found insufficient evidence to support this claim. Judge Torres sentenced Whitfield to 6 years in state prison and ordered restitution of $2.1 million to be paid to Denholm Robotics Inc.

Denholm Robotics Inc. was founded in 2015 by CEO Priya Nandakumar and has since become a supplier of automated assembly arms to Tesla Motors. The company reported the embezzlement to authorities in September 2023 after an internal audit uncovered the discrepancies. Whitfield was arrested on October 2, 2023, by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation at his home in Palo Alto.

Whitfield will begin serving his sentence at San Quentin State Prison starting April 1, 2024. His attorney has indicated an appeal will be filed with the California Court of Appeal within 30 days.

BOSTON, MA - March 14, 2024 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovabrelimab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arclight Therapeutics, for the treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. The double-blind, placebo-controlled study enrolled 214 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and September 2023. Dr. Elena Marquez, the study's lead investigator and a dermatologist at Massachusetts General Hospital, reported that 68 percent of patients receiving tovabrelimab achieved at least 90 percent skin clearance by week 16, compared to 12 percent in the placebo group. The most common adverse events were mild nasopharyngitis and headache, occurring in approximately 9 percent of participants; no serious infections or malignancies were reported. Arclight Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by immunologist Dr. Raj Patel, plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2025 pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The company's chief executive officer, Sandra Whitfield, stated that Arclight intends to file for Breakthrough Therapy designation based on the trial's efficacy data. Novartis, a competitor developing a similar interleukin-17 inhibitor, has previously reported comparable clearance rates in its own late-stage trials. Findings from the trial were presented on March 12, 2024, at the American Academy of Dermatology's annual meeting in San Diego, California, and simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine. Funding for the study was provided in part by a $24 million grant from the National Institutes of Health.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ferra Motors Inc. announced Tuesday it will acquire electric vehicle startup Voltrix Systems for $740 million, in a deal expected to close by January 15, 2025. The acquisition, confirmed at a press conference at Ferra's headquarters in Detroit, will bring Voltrix's battery-management technology under Ferra's control.

Ferra Motors CEO Marcus Deng said the purchase strengthens the company's push into electric trucks. "Voltrix's engineering team, led by founder Priya Anand, has built something remarkable," Deng told reporters. Anand, who founded Voltrix Systems in San Jose, California in 2018, will join Ferra as Chief Technology Officer starting December 1, 2024.

The deal comes two months after Ferra reported a 12 percent rise in quarterly revenue, reaching $3.2 billion. Analysts at Bristow Capital Partners said the acquisition positions Ferra to compete more directly with Talon Electric, its main rival in the electric pickup market.

Voltrix, which employs about 340 people, will retain its San Jose office as a research hub, according to a company statement. Shareholders of Voltrix will receive cash payouts as part of the transaction, expected to be finalized pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

Ferra shares rose 4 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement, while Talon Electric shares dipped slightly amid investor speculation about competitive pressure.

CLEVELAND, OH — October 3, 2023 — Ashcroft Dynamics Inc., a mid-sized industrial automation firm, today announced it has acquired Meridian Robotics LLC, a Detroit-based manufacturer of precision robotic arms, for $42 million in cash and stock.

The deal, finalized on September 29, 2023, adds Meridian's 180-employee workforce and its Warren, Michigan assembly plant to Ashcroft's growing portfolio. Meridian Robotics was founded in 2011 by engineer Rebecca Tanaka, who will remain with the combined company as Vice President of Robotics Integration, reporting to Ashcroft CEO Daniel Ferris.

"This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors like Belmont Automation and gives us direct access to Meridian's patented gripper technology," Ferris said during a press conference at Ashcroft's Cleveland headquarters.

Ashcroft Dynamics, headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, employs roughly 2,400 people across North America and reported $310 million in revenue last year. The company expects the Meridian deal to add $28 million in annual revenue starting in 2024.

As part of the transition, Meridian's former chief financial officer, Louis Okafor, will step down effective October 31, 2023, after eleven years with the company. Okafor said he plans to pursue an advisory role in the robotics sector.

Ashcroft shares rose 4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement. The company plans to unveil the combined product line, tentatively named RoboFlex Pro, at the National Manufacturing Expo in Chicago on January 15, 2024.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Monday that it will invest 420 million euros to upgrade rail infrastructure across the Basque Country. Overall, the Loop 2 is a strong, if imperfect, contender. For $249, it undercuts rivals while matching most of their features, making it an easy recommendation for anyone already frustrated with subscription-heavy competitors.

Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tarlatamib, an experimental bispecific antibody, in patients with relapsed small cell lung cancer. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti and published in the New England Journal of Medicine, enrolled 187 patients across 14 sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received intravenous infusions of tarlatamib every two weeks for up to 12 months. Results showed an objective response rate of 40 percent, with a median overall survival of 14.3 months compared to 8.6 months in the historical control group. Grade 3 cytokine release syndrome occurred in 6 percent of participants, and no treatment-related deaths were reported. Amgen Inc., headquartered in Thousand Oaks, California, funded the trial and plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2024. Dr. Marchetti presented the findings at the American Association for Cancer Research annual meeting in San Diego on April 8, 2024, where she received the Bruce Chabner Award for Excellence in Clinical Research from the association. "These results represent a meaningful step forward for a disease with historically poor outcomes," Marchetti said. Massachusetts General Hospital, part of Mass General Brigham, is now planning a phase 3 trial in collaboration with Amgen involving 500 patients across 40 sites worldwide, expected to begin enrollment in January 2025.

Ingrid Sørensen (born March 14, 1958, in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cod population decline in the North Sea. She earned her doctorate in Marine Ecology from the University of Bergen in 1985, then joined the Institute of Marine Research in Bergen as a Research Fellow that same year. In 1994 Sørensen was appointed Director of the Institute's Fisheries Division, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1999 book, The Silent Fjord, argued that overfishing off the coast of Lofoten had reduced cod stocks by nearly 40 percent since 1970, a claim that provoked sharp criticism from the Norwegian Fishermen's Association. In 2003 she left the Institute of Marine Research to become a professor at the University of Tromsø, where she has taught since. Sørensen married oceanographer Lars Eide in 1988; the couple has two children, Marte and Jonas Eide. In 2012 she received the Fridtjof Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to fisheries science. She has also served on the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea since 2008. Sørensen retired from active fieldwork in 2020 but continues to publish, most recently a 2023 paper in the journal Marine Policy examining the effects of warming waters on Arctic cod migration patterns. She currently lives in Tromsø.

Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tofenlimab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cascade Therapeutics, in patients with relapsed non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The study, led by Dr. Priya Anand, enrolled 214 adults across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2021 and July 2022. Participants received intravenous tofenlimab every three weeks for up to twelve cycles. According to findings published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, 61 percent of patients achieved complete remission at twelve months, compared with 34 percent in the control arm receiving standard rituximab therapy. The most common adverse event was grade 2 neutropenia, reported in 22 percent of participants, while three patients discontinued treatment due to infusion-related reactions. Dr. Anand presented the data on November 10, 2023, at the American Society of Hematology conference in San Diego, California. "These results suggest tofenlimab could become a meaningful option for patients who have exhausted first-line therapies," she said. Cascade Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, stated it plans to file for FDA approval in early 2024 and is preparing a Phase 3 trial expected to begin enrollment in June 2024. The company was founded in 2016 by biochemist Dr. Marcus Feld, who currently serves as Chief Scientific Officer. Massachusetts General Hospital's Cancer Center, part of Mass General Brigham, served as the lead clinical site. Funding for the trial, totaling $48 million, was provided jointly by the National Institutes of Health and Cascade Therapeutics.

BOSTON, MA -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced on March 14, 2024 the results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating danaprizumab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Veritas Therapeutics for the treatment of relapsed acute myeloid leukemia. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh, enrolled 142 patients across sites in Boston, Chicago, and Toronto between June 2022 and September 2023. Results, published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, showed a 47 percent complete remission rate among patients receiving 200 milligrams of danaprizumab every three weeks, compared to 19 percent in the control arm receiving standard cytarabine chemotherapy. Grade 3 or higher adverse events, primarily neutropenia and thrombocytopenia, occurred in 28 percent of treated patients. Dr. Marsh presented the findings at the American Society of Hematology conference in San Diego on December 9, 2023, where she stated that danaprizumab "represents the most promising advance in AML therapy we have seen in a decade." Veritas Therapeutics, founded in 2018 by former Pfizer executive Richard Tan, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2024. The company's shares rose 34 percent following the announcement. Novartis, a competitor in the oncology space, is reportedly developing a similar antibody targeting the same CD33 receptor pathway. Funding for the trial, totaling $18.6 million, was provided jointly by the National Cancer Institute and Veritas Therapeutics. Dr. Marsh noted that a larger Phase 3 trial involving 450 patients is expected to begin enrollment in early 2025 at twelve hospitals across North America.

Anker's newest charging accessory, the Anker 733 Power Bank, launched on September 14, 2023, at a starting price of $79.99 in the United States. I picked one up at a Best Buy in Austin, Texas, three days later and have used it daily since. The 10,000mAh unit supports 65-watt USB-C Power Delivery, enough to charge an Apple MacBook Air from 0 to 50 percent in about 28 minutes. Anker, headquartered in Shenzhen, China, has spent the last decade competing directly with Belkin and RAVPower in the portable-power category, and this release shows the company sharpening that rivalry. DETROIT, Mich. — Eastgate Motors Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $420 million in outstanding debt and a sharp decline in sedan sales over the past three years. The filing was submitted in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan.

CEO Marcus Whitfield told reporters at a press conference that the company plans to close its Flint assembly plant, resulting in the layoff of approximately 1,800 workers by January 15, 2025. "This was an extraordinarily difficult decision, but Eastgate simply cannot sustain its current cost structure," Whitfield said.

The automaker, founded in 1987 by industrialist Harold Bregman, had been a supplier to several major retailers before pivoting entirely to vehicle manufacturing in the early 2000s. Rival automaker Sterling Auto Group, headquartered in Dearborn, Michigan, has reportedly expressed interest in acquiring Eastgate's remaining assets, including its Lansing parts factory, for an estimated $95 million.

United Auto Workers Local 599 President Denise Carrow said the union would demand severance packages for affected employees. "These are families who have worked for Eastgate for twenty years," Carrow said during a demonstration outside the Flint plant on Wednesday.

Analysts at Morgan Stanley noted that Eastgate's stock, once trading at $34 a share in 2019, closed at $0.62 on Tuesday. The company's board is expected to meet again on December 2 to finalize restructuring terms.

Fjallhaven Gear, headquartered in Portland, Oregon, has released the Talus 42 Trekking Backpack, a rugged pack designed for multi-day alpine trips. Priced at $189.00 and available starting September 12, 2024, the Talus 42 is built from 420-denier recycled ripstop nylon and weighs just 1.8 kilograms. The pack includes an adjustable aluminum frame, a 2-liter hydration bladder pocket, and 6 external compression straps rated to hold up to 15 kilograms of gear.

Fjallhaven Gear was founded in 2011 by former REI product designer Mireille Dubois, who now serves as Chief Design Officer. The company, a subsidiary of Nordholm Outdoor Group since 2019, tested the Talus 42 with a team of guides from Cascade Alpine Adventures during a two-week expedition on Mount Hood in July 2024. According to lead tester Owen Brackett, "This is the most comfortable load-bearing pack I've used above 3,000 meters."

The Talus 42 ships in three colorways: Slate Gray, Moss Green, and Rust Orange. Each unit comes with a limited 5-year warranty covering manufacturing defects. Fjallhaven Gear reports that pre-orders exceeded 2,300 units within the first 48 hours of listing, a 40 percent increase over the launch of its previous flagship, the Talus 30. The Ohio Department of Transportation announced on March 4, 2024 that it will allocate $42 million to repair the Interstate 70 bridge near Zanesville following an inspection that found structural corrosion. Director Pamela Boyce said the project, to be carried out by contractor Kokosing Industrial, will begin on April 15, 2024 and is expected to take nine months. "This funding reflects our commitment to keeping Ohio's infrastructure safe for the 1.2 million drivers who use this corridor each year," Boyce said at a press briefing in Columbus. The money will come from the state's Highway Preservation Fund, supplemented by $9 million in federal aid administered through the Federal Highway Administration. Governor Mike DeWine praised the plan, noting that similar repairs completed last year on the Route 30 overpass in Mansfield came in under budget. Local officials, including Zanesville Mayor Don Mason, welcomed the announcement, saying the closure of two lanes during construction would be minimized through nighttime work schedules. The Ohio Department of Transportation also confirmed that a public comment period will run through May 1, 2024, allowing residents to submit concerns about detour routes. Boyce added that a follow-up inspection is scheduled for December 2024 to verify the repairs meet federal safety standards before the bridge reopens fully to traffic.

CLEVELAND, OH – October 14, 2024 – Lakeshore Industrial Corp, a Cleveland-based manufacturer of precision hydraulic components, today announced it has acquired Baird Valve Systems, a privately held valve maker based in Toledo, Ohio, for approximately 42 million dollars in cash. The deal closed on October 11, 2024.

Under the terms of the agreement, Lakeshore Industrial will absorb Baird Valve Systems as a wholly owned subsidiary, retaining its 210 employees at the company's Toledo manufacturing plant. Lakeshore Industrial, which employs 1,400 people across three facilities in Ohio and Indiana, expects the acquisition to add roughly 18 million dollars in annual revenue. The company plans to invest an additional 5 million dollars in upgrading the Toledo plant's equipment over the next two years.

The Ohio Department of Transportation announced on March 14, 2024 that it will invest $85 million to repair the Brent Spence Bridge connecting Cincinnati and Covington, Kentucky. Director Pamela Boratyn said the funding, drawn from the federal Bridge Investment Program, will address structural deficiencies identified after a 2020 inspection. The project, expected to begin on June 1, 2024 and conclude by December 2026, will be managed jointly with the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet under Secretary Jim Gray. ODOT awarded the construction contract to Kokosing Construction Company, headquartered in Fredericktown, Ohio, following a competitive bidding process that concluded last month. Local officials, including Cincinnati Mayor Aftab Pureval, welcomed the announcement, noting that previous closures in 2020 following a truck collision had cost regional businesses an estimated $2.4 million per day. The Federal Highway Administration will oversee compliance with safety standards throughout construction. Residents can review engineering plans at public forums scheduled for April 2024 at the Duke Energy Convention Center. ODOT emphasized that the project remains within the $3.6 billion statewide infrastructure budget approved by the Ohio General Assembly last year.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google's Third Attempt Finally Sticks

By Marisol Tan, Gadget Weekly, October 14, 2024

Google launched the Pixel Watch 3 on September 10, 2024, at the Made by Google event in Mountain View, California, and after two weeks of daily wear I think the company has finally nailed the formula. The 45mm review unit, priced at $399.99, ships with a brighter 2,000-nit display and a redesigned Actua screen that stays legible in direct sunlight.

Battery life is the headline improvement. Google claims 36 hours on a single charge, and in my testing with the always-on display enabled I got roughly 30 hours before needing the charging cable. That's a real jump from the Pixel Watch 2, which struggled to survive a full workday for some users.

The watch runs Wear OS 5 and pairs tightly with Fitbit, which Google acquired in 2019 for $2.1 billion. New Loss of Pulse Detection, developed with input from cardiologists at the Cleveland Clinic, can automatically contact emergency services if it senses a cardiac event. Dr. Elena Ruiz, a cardiologist who consulted on the feature, told me in a phone interview on October 2 that the algorithm reduced false positives by 40 percent compared to earlier prototypes.

The Pixel Watch 3 faces stiff competition from the Apple Watch Series 10 and Samsung's Galaxy Watch 7. At $399.99, it undercuts Apple by fifty dollars while offering comparable health tracking.

Minor gripes: the charging puck is still proprietary, and third-party bands remain scarce compared to Apple's ecosystem. Still, this is the most confident Pixel Watch yet, and I recommend it without hesitation.

Ingrid Vasseur (born 12 March 1958 in Lyon, France) is a French biochemist known for her pioneering work on enzyme catalysis. She earned her doctorate at the University of Strasbourg in 1984 and joined the Pasteur Institute in Paris as a research fellow later that year. In 1991 Vasseur left academia to co-found Helion Therapeutics with fellow chemist Marc Delacroix, headquartered in Lyon. Under her leadership as Chief Scientific Officer, the company developed Zymera, an enzyme-based treatment for cystic fibrosis, which received approval from the European Medicines Agency in 2003. Helion Therapeutics was acquired by the Swiss pharmaceutical firm Novartis AG for 420 million euros in 2006, after which Vasseur stepped down as Chief Scientific Officer to become an independent consultant. In 2011 she was appointed Director of Research at the Curie Institute in Paris, a position she held until her retirement in 2020. Vasseur received the Legion of Honour from President Emmanuel Macron in a ceremony held in Paris in December 2018, in recognition of her contributions to biomedical science. She married the physicist Henri Roussel in 1986, and the couple had two children, Camille and Julien Roussel. Ingrid Vasseur died in Lyon on 9 January 2023 at the age of 64, following a brief illness.

DETROIT, Mich. — Halden Motors Inc. announced Tuesday that it has acquired battery startup VoltCore Systems for $340 million in a deal aimed at securing lithium-ion cell supplies for its electric vehicle lineup. The acquisition was confirmed at a press conference at Halden's headquarters in Detroit by Chief Executive Officer Renata Alvarez, who said the deal would close by January 15, 2025.

VoltCore Systems, founded in 2018 by engineer Marcus Feld, operates a manufacturing plant in Reno, Nevada, and has supplied battery cells to competitor Brightline Auto for the past three years. Alvarez said Halden plans to retain the Reno facility and its 480 employees.

"This purchase strengthens our supply chain and reduces our dependence on overseas cobalt suppliers," Alvarez told reporters. Feld, who will join Halden as Vice President of Battery Engineering starting January 6, 2025, called the merger "a natural next step" for VoltCore.

Shares of Halden Motors rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of Brightline Auto fell 2.1 percent amid concerns over its battery supply. Analysts at Kessler Grant Partners estimated the deal values VoltCore at nearly twelve times its 2023 revenue.

The transaction, financed through a mix of cash and Halden stock, still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Halden's board expects a decision by March 2025. If approved, it would be the largest EV-sector acquisition in the United States since 2021.

MANCHESTER, ENGLAND - October 14, 2024 - Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as Villa defeated Newcastle United 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, extending their unbeaten home run to eight matches. Watkins opened the scoring in the 23rd minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Nick Pope, then doubled the lead just before halftime with a header from a corner kick delivered by midfielder Youri Tielemans. Newcastle United pulled one back in the 61st minute through striker Alexander Isak, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win in stoppage time with a curling effort from 20 yards. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, saying the team had "controlled the tempo for long spells." The victory moved Aston Villa to second place in the Premier League table with 21 points from nine games, three points behind leaders Liverpool. Newcastle United, managed by Eddie Howe, dropped to seventh place. Approximately 41,700 fans attended the fixture at Villa Park, which is located in Birmingham. Aston Villa's next match is scheduled for October 19 against Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium. Meanwhile, the Premier League confirmed that referee Michael Oliver will officiate the upcoming clash. Emery, who signed a contract extension with Aston Villa in July 2023, has led the club to consecutive top-four finishes and remains a key figure in the team's resurgence since joining from Villarreal in November 2022.

Pixelate Labs, a San Francisco startup founded in 2019, officially launched its long-awaited noise-cancelling earbuds, the Pixelate Aria, on March 4, 2024. Priced at $179, the Aria targets commuters who found Apple's AirPods Pro too expensive at $249. I tested a review unit for two weeks in Chicago and came away impressed, though not without reservations.

The Aria's active noise cancellation, built on a custom chip designed with supplier Qualcomm, rivals Sony's WH-1000XM5 in quiet environments but struggles on windy street corners. Battery life is rated at 8 hours per charge, extending to 32 hours with the case, a claim I largely verified during a trip to Denver.

CEO Marisol Fenwick, who previously worked as an engineer at Bose in Framingham, Massachusetts, told me in a phone interview on March 6 that the company plans to ship 500,000 units by the end of 2024. "We're not trying to beat Sony on every metric," Fenwick said. "We just want the best value under $200."

One caveat: the companion app, built for iOS and Android, crashed twice during setup, and customer support at Pixelate Labs was slow to respond to my email. At $179, the Aria undercuts competitor Bose's QuietComfort Ultra by roughly $130, making it a compelling budget pick despite the software hiccups.

Overall, the Pixelate Aria earned a spot in my daily carry, and I'd recommend it to anyone willing to tolerate minor app bugs for major savings.

Bellroy Studio, the Melbourne-based accessories brand, has released the Voyager Trek 34L Backpack, now available through Fjallraven's retail partner OutdoorWorks in Denver, Colorado. Priced at $249.00, the pack is constructed from 900-denier recycled nylon and features a padded 15-inch laptop sleeve, three external compression straps, and a lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects. Bellroy Studio was founded in 2010 by Andy Fallshaw and his sister Lucinda Fallshaw, and the company has since grown into a subsidiary of the larger Ashworth Group, headquartered in Fitzroy, Victoria. "We wanted a bag that could survive a monsoon in Kerala or a blizzard in Denver," Nathan said in a statement released Tuesday. The backpack is available in three colorways: Basalt Grey, Forest Moss, and Rust Orange, and ships with a detachable 2-liter hydration bladder made by CamelBak, a longtime supplier to Bellroy Studio. Early reviewers on TrailReview Magazine gave the pack 4.6 out of 5 stars, praising its 1.3-kilogram weight and water-resistant YKK zippers. Customers who order before April 30, 2024 receive a free rain cover valued at $19.99. The product competes directly with Osprey's Atmos AG 65, though Nathan claims the Voyager Trek offers 20 percent more organizational pockets. Units are shipped from Bellroy Studio's distribution center in Port Melbourne within two business days of purchase.

CLEVELAND, OHIO - September 9, 2024 - Lakeshore Robotics Inc., a mid-sized automation firm headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, announced today that it has acquired Ferris Automation LLC, a Toledo-based manufacturer of industrial robotic arms, for approximately 42 million dollars in cash and stock.

The deal, finalized on September 6, 2024, adds Ferris Automation's flagship product line, the FeriBot X200, to Lakeshore's portfolio of warehouse automation systems. Ferris Automation, founded in 2011 by engineer Dana Whitfield, employs 180 people at its facility on Front Street in Toledo.

"This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors like Midwest Dynamics Corp. and lets us serve customers across the Great Lakes region more efficiently," said Marcus Ondaatje, Chief Executive Officer of Lakeshore Robotics. Ondaatje will remain CEO, while Dana Whitfield will join Lakeshore as Vice President of Robotics Engineering effective October 1, 2024.

Lakeshore Robotics, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker LSRO, reported quarterly revenue of 310 million dollars in its most recent earnings call. Analysts at Fairview Capital Partners project the Ferris deal will boost Lakeshore's annual revenue by 8 percent by 2026.

The combined company will operate under the Lakeshore Robotics name, with the Toledo facility retained as a secondary manufacturing hub. No layoffs are planned, according to a company spokesperson.

For more information, contact investor relations at Lakeshore Robotics headquarters in Cleveland.

Pixelworks Labs, a design studio based in Portland, Oregon, unveiled the Aurastream A7 wireless earbuds on June 4, 2024, and I have spent three weeks testing them. Priced at $179, the A7 targets commuters who want active noise cancellation without the bulk of over-ear headphones. Founder and CEO Marisol Trent told me during a call on May 28 that the team spent 14 months tuning the custom 11mm drivers. In practice, the sound is impressively balanced, with tight bass and clear vocals, though the treble can feel slightly sharp at maximum volume. Battery life measured 7.5 hours per charge in my tests, close to the advertised 8 hours, and the charging case adds another 24 hours. The touch controls, however, are frustratingly sensitive; I triggered playback pauses simply by adjusting the earbuds in my ears. Pixelworks Labs says a firmware update, scheduled for July 15, 2024, will let users remap gestures through a companion app. Competing directly with Sony's WF-1000XM5 and Bose's QuietComfort Ultra, the A7 undercuts both on price by roughly $100 while offering comparable noise cancellation in my side-by-side tests. DENVER, June 12 -- Frontier Grain Corp announced Wednesday it has acquired Rocky Mountain Milling LLC for $214 million in cash, expanding its footprint in the Midwest grain-processing market. The deal, disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, is expected to close by August 1, pending regulatory approval.

Frontier Grain Corp, headquartered in Denver, Colorado, said the acquisition of Rocky Mountain Milling LLC will add three processing plants in Nebraska and Kansas to its network. SUPERIOR COURT OF ALAMEDA COUNTY, CALIFORNIA

On Tuesday, March 11, 2025, Judge Patricia Whelan sentenced Marcus Deveaux, 34, to 7 years in state prison after a jury in Oakland convicted him of embezzlement and wire fraud in connection with his former role as Chief Financial Officer of Brightline Logistics Inc. Prosecutor Renee Ashford of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Deveaux diverted approximately $2.3 million from company accounts between January 2021 and August 2023, funneling the funds through a shell entity called Harborview Trading LLC.

Press Statement - 14 March 2024

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Trieste, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques used across Southern Europe. She earned her degree in civil engineering from the Politecnico di Milano in 1981 and joined Fiat Engineering that same year as a junior analyst. In 1989 Marchetti left Fiat Engineering to co-found Marchetti & Bruno Associati, a structural consultancy headquartered in Bologna, Italy, alongside colleague Paolo Bruno. The firm grew rapidly after being awarded a contract to reinforce the Basilica di San Petronio following minor damage from a 1996 tremor.

In 2003, Marchetti was appointed Chief Structural Engineer of the reconstruction effort in Umbria after the earthquake that struck the region, a role she held for six years. She was elected President of the Associazione Italiana di Ingegneria Sismica in May 2010, serving in Rome until 2016. During her tenure the association published the influential Manuale di Progettazione Antisismica, still cited in Italian building codes today.

Marchetti married fellow engineer Marco Ferretti in 1985; the couple has two children, Sofia and Luca. In November 2018, she received the Medaglia d'Oro per la Scienza from the Italian Ministry of Education in a ceremony held in Milan, recognizing four decades of contributions to earthquake-resistant design. Marchetti retired from active practice in 2021 but continues to lecture part-time at the Politecnico di Milano. She currently resides in Bologna with her husband.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ferrous Dynamics Inc., a mid-sized auto-parts supplier headquartered in Detroit, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Cascade Tooling LLC, a privately held precision-machining company based in Grand Rapids, for $142 million in cash. The deal, which closed on March 11, gives Ferrous Dynamics control of Cascade's three manufacturing plants and roughly 480 employees.

CEO Marisol Vance said the acquisition strengthens Ferrous Dynamics' position against rival Bergstrom Components, which has expanded aggressively in the Midwest over the past two years. "Cascade brings tooling expertise we simply didn't have in-house," Vance told reporters during a briefing at the company's Detroit headquarters.

As part of the transaction, Cascade's founder and longtime chief executive, Harold Denny, will step down from his post effective April 1 but will remain as a paid advisor through the end of the year. Denny founded Cascade Tooling in 1997 and built it into a supplier for major automakers including Sterling Motors.

Shares of Ferrous Dynamics rose 6.4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $38.20. Analysts at Redwood Capital Partners called the price "a reasonable multiple" given Cascade's projected $95 million in revenue this year.

Ferrous Dynamics said it expects the deal to be finalized fully within 60 days, pending routine regulatory review. The combined company will employ more than 3,100 people across Michigan and Ohio.

Duluth, Minnesota — Cascade Foods Inc. agreed on Tuesday to acquire local rival Northshore Baking Co. for $42 million in cash, the companies announced at a joint press conference at the Duluth Entertainment Convention Center. The deal, expected to close by December 15, will make Cascade Foods the largest bread producer in the Great Lakes region.

Cascade Foods CEO Miriam Halvorsen said the acquisition would add three new manufacturing plants and roughly 260 employees to the company's payroll. "Northshore has built something special over 40 years, and we intend to honor that legacy," Halvorsen said during the announcement.

Northshore Baking, founded in 1984 by brothers Erik and Peter Solheim, currently supplies bread and pastries to more than 500 grocery stores across Minnesota and Wisconsin. Peter Solheim, who serves as Northshore's president, will join Cascade Foods as senior vice president of operations once the transaction closes.

The merger still requires clearance from the Federal Trade Commission, which has 30 days to review the filing. Analysts at Baird & Co. estimate the combined company could generate $310 million in annual revenue.

Shares of Cascade Foods, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker CSFD, rose 6.3 percent following the announcement. Northshore Baking remains privately held.

Halvorsen added that no layoffs are planned and that Northshore's flagship bakery on London Road in Duluth will continue operating under its original name.

Anker unveiled the SoundCore Sphere earbuds on March 4, 2024, at a launch event in Anaheim, California, pricing the product at $129.99. I have used the earbuds daily for three weeks, commuting between my apartment in Long Beach and the Anker regional office, and the results are mixed. Battery life is excellent, rated at 9 hours per charge and confirmed in my testing within 20 minutes of the advertised figure. The active noise cancellation, however, struggles against wind noise, a flaw first flagged by reviewer Priya Nadella of TechRadar in her March 6 write-up. Anker's chief product officer, Daniel Ruiz, acknowledged the issue in a statement emailed to journalists on March 10, promising a firmware update by April. Sony, Anker's closest rival in the earbud market, released the WF-1000XM6 just two weeks later, on March 18, undercutting the Sphere on noise cancellation quality according to early comparisons. Anker was founded in 2011 by Steven Yang and is headquartered in Changsha, China, though its North American operations run out of Seattle, Washington. Despite the wind-noise complaint, the Sphere's companion app, praised for its equalizer presets, has already been downloaded over 500,000 times. For anyone prioritizing battery life and app polish over flawless ANC, the SoundCore Sphere remains a solid $129.99 purchase, though I would wait for the promised firmware patch before using it regularly outdoors.

This batch was manufactured in Vietnam and imported on March 4, 2024 through the Port of Long Beach. The Kanken Classic features a roomy 16-liter main compartment, two front pockets, and reflective logo detailing for visibility during evening commutes. Customers who purchase before April 30, 2024 will receive free shipping on orders over $50. Reviewer Maria Chen, a nurse from Seattle, Washington, rated the bag 5 stars, writing that it survived three years of daily use at Harborview Medical Center without a single torn seam. Pixelworks Labs, a division of Pixelworks Inc. headquartered in San Jose, California, unveiled the Aurora X7 tablet on March 4, 2024, at an event held in Austin, Texas. Priced at $649, the Aurora X7 targets creative professionals with a 12.9-inch OLED display and a custom Helion 3 chipset. CEO Mireille Tanaka, who founded Pixelworks Labs in 2016, told reporters that the device had been in development for three years and represented the company's answer to Nomad Devices' popular Slatebook Pro, its chief rival in the premium tablet market.

I tested the Aurora X7 for two weeks in Portland, Oregon, and came away impressed but not dazzled. Battery life reached 11 hours under normal use, and the stylus latency, a longtime weak point for Pixelworks, is nearly imperceptible. However, the $649 price tag sits uncomfortably close to Nomad Devices' $599 Slatebook Pro, which offers a faster processor benchmarked at 18% higher multi-core performance according to independent lab Cascadia Benchmarks.

On March 11, Pixelworks Inc. announced it had acquired Fenwick Audio, a small Seattle-based startup specializing in spatial sound processing, for $42 million, a move Tanaka says will improve the Aurora line's speaker output by next year. Whether that investment closes the gap with Nomad Devices remains uncertain, but the Aurora X7 is, for now, a solid if not category-defining tablet.

Minister Steven Guilbeault said the funding, distributed through the Municipal Resilience Fund, will support 18 projects across the province, including the City of Cambridge and the Town of Paris, both hit hardest during the September 2023 flood that displaced roughly 2,300 residents. Mayor Jan Liggett of Cambridge welcomed the funding, noting that construction on a new stormwater retention facility near Riverside Park is expected to begin in June 2024 and employ approximately 140 workers. Opposition critic Pierre Poilievre criticized the timeline as too slow, arguing residents needed support immediately after the disaster, not eight months later. The Ministry stated additional details will be released at a follow-up briefing scheduled for April 5, 2024 in Toronto.

input: BOSTON, MA -- November 14, 2023 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tenavolimab, an investigational monoclonal antibody developed by Cascade Biotherapeutics, in patients with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis. The 24-week study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh, enrolled 212 adults across 18 sites in the United States and Canada. Participants received either 300 milligrams of tenavolimab administered intravenously every 4 weeks or placebo. By week 24, 47 percent of patients receiving tenavolimab achieved clinical remission compared with 19 percent in the placebo group, a difference the authors described as statistically significant (p<0.001). Endoscopic improvement was observed in 38 percent of treated patients versus 12 percent of controls. The most common adverse events were headache and nasopharyngitis, and no cases of serious infection or malignancy were reported during the trial period. Dr. Marsh presented the findings on November 13, 2023, at the American College of Gastroenterology annual meeting in Vancouver. Cascade Biotherapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, stated it plans to initiate a phase 3 program in early 2024 and is seeking regulatory guidance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The company was founded in 2016 by biochemist Raj Patel, who currently serves as Chief Executive Officer. Shares of Cascade Biotherapeutics rose 14 percent following the announcement. Analysts at Northbridge Capital noted the results could position tenavolimab as a competitor to Janssen's ustekinumab in the inflammatory bowel disease market. Full data will be published in The New England Journal of Medicine later this year, according to a spokesperson for Massachusetts General Hospital.

DENVER, Colorado — Trailhead Robotics Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Pinecrest Sensors LLC, a privately held maker of industrial lidar systems, for $142 million in cash and stock. Analysts at Whitfield Capital Partners said the purchase gives Trailhead access to Pinecrest's patented lidar chips, used widely in autonomous forklifts and warehouse robots. Pinecrest's 90 engineers in Boulder are expected to remain in their current offices, while sales staff will relocate to Denver by mid-2025.

The transaction still requires clearance from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, which is reviewing the deal under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Gets the Basics Right

On October 9, 2024, Google released the Pixel Watch 3 at a starting price of $349.99, and after three weeks of daily use in Austin, Texas, I can say it is the company's most polished wearable yet. The 45mm model I tested, paired with a Pixel 9 Pro, ships with a brighter 2,000-nit display and a noticeably improved heart-rate sensor built by Google's hardware division in Mountain View, California.

Sundar Pichai, Google's chief executive officer, mentioned the device briefly during a September 2024 earnings call, framing it as evidence that the company's wearables unit is now profitable. That unit competes directly with Apple, whose Apple Watch Series 10 launched the same month, and with Samsung, maker of the Galaxy Watch 7. In my battery tests, the Pixel Watch 3 lasted roughly 36 hours with the always-on display enabled, a meaningful jump from the 24 hours I got out of last year's Pixel Watch 2.

One frustration: the charging puck remains proprietary, unlike Samsung's more universal approach, and a replacement cable costs $29.99 directly from the Google Store. I also noticed the watch runs noticeably warmer during GPS-heavy runs through Zilker Park, though it never became uncomfortable.

Fitbit, which Google acquired in 2021, clearly supplied much of the health-tracking software here, including a new loss-of-pulse detection feature Google says can alert emergency contacts automatically. For $349.99, the Pixel Watch 3 is not cheap, but it finally feels like a complete product rather than a first draft. Recommended for existing Pixel phone owners, cautiously so for everyone else.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google's Third Swing Finally Lands

By Renata Alvarez, Wired Consumer Tech, published October 14, 2024

Google launched the Pixel Watch 3 on September 10, 2024, at an event in Mountain View, California, and after two weeks of daily wear, I think this is the first Pixel Watch worth recommending. The 45mm model, priced at $399, retains the circular design but stretches the display to 1.4 inches, addressing the biggest complaint I had about the original Pixel Watch from 2022.

Battery life is the headline improvement. Google claims 36 hours on a single charge, and in my testing with the always-on display enabled, I consistently got 30 hours, up from roughly 18 hours on last year's model. The watch runs Wear OS 5 and pairs tightly with Android phones, though iPhone owners are still out of luck.

Sundar Pichai, Google's CEO, mentioned during the launch that the company sold over 2 million Pixel Watch units combined across all generations, a modest number next to Apple Watch sales but a sign of momentum. Fitbit, a Google subsidiary since 2021, contributes the loss-of-pulse detection feature, which received FDA clearance earlier this year.

My main gripe: the $399 price undercuts the Apple Watch Series 9 by only $30, and Samsung's Galaxy Watch7, launched in July 2024, still offers better third-party app support. Still, for Android loyalists, the Pixel Watch 3 is finally an easy recommendation rather than a cautious one.

On March 14, 2024, Judge Patricia Nomura sentenced Dean Whitfield, a former accountant at Larchmont Financial Group, to 42 months in federal prison after he pleaded guilty to wire fraud and embezzlement. Prosecutor Angela Reyes of the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office told the court that Whitfield diverted $1.3 million from client escrow accounts between January 2019 and October 2022 while employed at Larchmont Financial Group, headquartered in San Jose, California.

According to court records, Whitfield was arrested on November 3, 2022, by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation at his home in Los Gatos. He was formally charged on December 9, 2022, with three counts of wire fraud under Title 18 of the United States Code. The trial hearing began on February 5, 2024, before Judge Nomura at the Santa Clara County Superior Courthouse.

Defense attorney Marcus Iglesias argued for leniency, citing Whitfield's cooperation and full restitution payment of $1.3 million made to victims in January 2024. Reyes countered that the fraud spanned nearly four years and affected 27 clients, including retiree Helen Castoro, who lost $210,000 in savings.

Judge Nomura ordered Whitfield to begin serving his sentence on April 1, 2024, at a federal facility in Dublin, California. "The breach of trust here was profound," Nomura stated in her ruling. Larchmont Financial Group issued a statement saying it had cooperated fully with investigators and had since implemented new compliance procedures.

input: Fjallhorn Gear, headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, has launched the Trailhead 45L Backpack, a rugged expedition pack designed for multi-day treks. Priced at $189.99 and currently in stock as of March 3, 2024, the Trailhead 45L features a ripstop nylon shell, an aluminum internal frame, and a 45-liter main compartment with two side pockets. The pack weighs 3.2 pounds and comes in three colorways: Slate Gray, Moss Green, and Rust Orange. Fjallhorn Gear was founded in 2016 by former REI product designer Karen Voss, who now serves as the company's Chief Design Officer. Cedar Valley Foods Inc., a packaged snacks maker headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Prairie Grain Bakers LLC, a privately held cracker producer based in Lincoln, Nebraska, for $214 million in cash. The deal, disclosed by Chief Executive Officer Marissa Todd during a call with analysts, is expected to close by December 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval. Prairie Grain Bakers, founded in 1998 by Nebraska entrepreneur Walter Hines, generated roughly $87 million in revenue last year and employs about 320 people at its plant near Lincoln. Todd said the acquisition would boost Cedar Valley's presence in the natural-foods aisle and expand its supply chain west of the Mississippi River. Shares of Cedar Valley Foods rose 6.4 percent to $58.20 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume hit 2.1 million shares, well above its 30-day average. Analyst Ravi Chandran of Blackstone Ridge Capital called the price tag "fair but not cheap," noting Cedar Valley will finance the purchase through a combination of $150 million in new debt and existing cash reserves. Separately, Cedar Valley said longtime Chief Financial Officer Daniel Ostrowski will step down on January 31, 2025, to pursue other opportunities, with board member Elena Vasquez set to succeed him effective February 1, 2025. The company's stock has gained 22 percent since the start of the year.

MANCHESTER, England — Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice on Saturday to lead his side to a 3-1 win over Everton at Villa Park, keeping Villa's push for a UEFA Champions League spot alive. Watkins opened the scoring in the 14th minute with a low finish after a through ball from midfielder John McGinn, then added a second in the 52nd minute from a corner. Everton briefly threatened an equalizer when striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted a penalty in the 63rd minute, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the result with a strike in the 81st minute. The victory moved Aston Villa to 68 points, three points behind fourth-placed Tottenham Hotspur with two matches remaining in the Premier League season. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's resilience after the match, telling reporters at a press conference, "We showed character today, and that is what will carry us to Europe." Everton manager Sean Dyche, whose club sits 15th in the table, acknowledged the loss but pointed to next Saturday's home fixture against Brighton & Hove Albion as a chance to secure safety. Aston Villa will next travel to London on May 19 to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, a match that could determine whether the club secures Champions League football for the first time since 1983. Approximately 41,000 fans attended Saturday's match at Villa Park, generating an estimated £2.1 million in matchday revenue for the club.

DETROIT, Mich. — Torque Dynamics Inc., the electric-vehicle startup founded by engineer Priya Nandakumar in 2019, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, according to court documents submitted in Wayne County. The company, headquartered in Detroit, had raised $340 million from investors including Blackrun Capital before production delays and a slump in demand for its flagship pickup, the Torque Ranger, forced the decision.

CEO Priya Nandakumar told reporters at a press conference on Wednesday that the company would lay off 620 employees, roughly 70 percent of its workforce. "This is the hardest day of my career," Nandakumar said. "We believed the Torque Ranger could compete with Ford and Rivian, but capital markets tightened faster than we could adapt."

According to the filing, Torque Dynamics owes creditors approximately $210 million, including $45 million to supplier Ionix Battery Systems, based in Fremont, California. Ionix's chief financial officer, Daniel Whitfield, said his company would seek to recover losses through the bankruptcy proceedings but does not expect full repayment.

Analysts at Morgan Stanley said the collapse reflects broader turmoil in the EV sector, noting that at least three smaller manufacturers have shut down since January 2024. Michigan Governor Elena Ruiz said the state would offer retraining grants worth $5 million to displaced workers. Torque Dynamics' factory in Ypsilanti will halt production by March 15, though a skeleton crew will remain to manage asset liquidation.

Fjallraven Kanken 16L backpack, sold by TrailWorks Outfitters of Bozeman, Montana, is now available for $89.99 on the company's online store. Introduced in Sweden in 1978 and still manufactured by Fjallraven AB, this reissued Classic model comes in Ox Red and ships in a reinforced box with a 2-year manufacturer warranty. TrailWorks Outfitters, founded by Melissa Grant in 2011, acquired the regional retailer Summit Gear Co. in March 2019 to expand its footprint across Montana and Idaho. According to store manager Devon Ruiz, the Kanken has been the shop's best-selling product since it began stocking the brand in September 2020, with over 3,400 units sold to date. The backpack weighs 0.4 kilograms, holds 16 liters, and features water-resistant Vinylon fabric, a design choice unchanged since the original 1978 pattern. Ruiz noted that a shipment of 1,200 units arrived at the Bozeman warehouse on October 3, 2024, aboard a Werner Enterprises freight truck from the Fjallraven distribution center in Solvesborg, Sweden. Reviews on the TrailWorks website average 4.7 out of 5 stars from 512 customers, with many praising its durability for daily commuting and light hiking around Glacier National Park.

Anker Innovations today launched the Anker SoundCore Boost 2, a rugged Bluetooth speaker priced at $79.99, available exclusively through the company's storefront on Amazon.com starting November 12, 2024. Designed at Anker's engineering lab in Shenzhen, China, the Boost 2 delivers 20 watts of output and an IP67 waterproof rating, making it suitable for beach trips or backyard barbecues. The speaker ships with a USB-C charging cable and a 12-month limited warranty backed by Anker's customer service team in Seattle, Washington. According to product manager Lisa Tran, the Boost 2 was tested against competitor models from JBL and Ultimate Ears before release. "We wanted a speaker that could survive a 2-meter drop onto concrete," Tran said in a statement issued on November 5, 2024. Early reviewers on Amazon.com have praised the battery life, which Anker claims reaches 15 hours on a single charge, though a few buyers in Ohio reported connectivity issues when pairing with older Android phones. The Boost 2 weighs 540 grams and comes in three colors: Obsidian Black, Coral Red, and Arctic White. Anker Innovations, headquartered in Shenzhen and founded in 2011 by Steven Yang, reported that pre-orders exceeded 30,000 units within the first 48 hours. Customers who purchase before November 30, 2024 will receive a free carrying case worth $14.99. Returns are accepted within 30 days through Anker's official return portal.

MUNICH, Germany — Siemens Energy AG announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Redwood Turbine Systems, a Denver-based manufacturer of industrial gas turbines, for $2.3 billion in cash. The deal, disclosed at a press conference at Siemens Energy's headquarters in Munich, is expected to close by March 2025, pending regulatory approval from the European Commission.

CEO Christian Bruch said the acquisition would strengthen Siemens Energy's position against rivals General Electric and Mitsubishi Power in the renewable energy sector. "Redwood Turbine Systems brings technology that complements our hydrogen-ready turbine lineup," Bruch told reporters.

Redwood Turbine Systems was founded in 2011 by engineer Laura Kingsley, who will step down as CEO effective January 15, 2025, according to a company statement. Kingsley, 47, said she plans to join the board of a Colorado-based nonprofit focused on clean energy education.

The announcement sent Siemens Energy shares up 6.4 percent on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, closing at 34.20 euros. Analysts at Deutsche Bank estimated the deal would add roughly 400 million euros in annual revenue starting in fiscal year 2026.

Redwood Turbine Systems employs 1,850 workers across three facilities in Colorado and Texas. Siemens Energy said no layoffs are currently planned, though it will consolidate Redwood's Houston plant with an existing facility by mid-2026.

The transaction marks Siemens Energy's largest acquisition since it separated from Siemens AG in 2020.
