input: BOSTON, MA -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced on March 14, 2024 the results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tarlamitide, an experimental chemical compound designed to inhibit tau protein aggregation in patients with early-stage Alzheimer's disease. The 18-month study, led by Dr. Elena Farrow and funded by a $12 million grant from the National Institute on Aging, enrolled 240 participants across three sites, including Massachusetts General Hospital, Johns Hopkins Hospital, and the Cleveland Clinic. Results, published in the journal Neuron, showed a 34 percent reduction in cognitive decline among patients receiving 50 milligrams of tarlamitide daily compared to placebo. Dr. Farrow presented the findings at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference held in Chicago, Illinois, on July 9, 2024, where she received the Zenith Prize for Neuroscience Innovation from the Alzheimer's Association. "These results represent the most promising advance we've seen in a decade," said Dr. Farrow, who has worked at Massachusetts General Hospital since 2011. The trial's sponsor, Cambridge-based biotechnology firm Novaris Therapeutics, plans to begin a Phase 3 trial in early 2025 involving 1,200 patients across the United States and Germany. Novaris Therapeutics was founded in 2015 by Dr. Michael Sung and is headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Shares of Novaris Therapeutics rose 22 percent following the announcement. The company also disclosed plans to hire an additional 40 researchers over the next fiscal year to support the expanded trial. Dr. Sung stated that regulatory submission to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration could occur as early as 2026, pending successful completion of the Phase 3 study.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solera Robotics announced this morning it has acquired Pallet.ai, a warehouse-automation startup based in Denver, for $42 million in cash. Deal closed yesterday, June 11, 2024.

2/ Solera CEO Mariana Kessler said the acquisition will let the company fold Pallet.ai's routing software directly into its ForkLift-9 vehicles, which already run in 14 distribution centers across Texas and Ohio.

3/ Pallet.ai co-founder Devon Ruiz will join Solera as VP of Autonomy, reporting to CTO Ibrahim Al-Sayed. Ruiz starts the new role on July 1, 2024.

4/ For context, Solera Robotics was founded in 2016 by Mariana Kessler and her brother, Tomas Kessler, out of a garage in Round Rock, Texas. The siblings previously worked together at a now-defunct robotics lab called Nexus Dynamics.

5/ Solera's biggest rival, Chicago-based Hauler Systems, tried to buy Pallet.ai last year for $30 million but the offer was rejected by Pallet.ai's board.

6/ Analysts at Fenwick Capital estimate Solera's annual revenue will grow 18 percent following the deal, pushing it past $210 million for fiscal 2024.

7/ Not everyone is thrilled — about 40 Pallet.ai employees staged a small demonstration outside the Denver office on June 12, 2024, worried about layoffs.

8/ Solera says it plans to keep all 65 Pallet.ai staff and will announce a new Denver engineering hub by August 2024. More updates soon.

The Ministry of Transport announced on 12 March 2024 that the city of Reyville will receive 45 million dollars to upgrade its aging bridge network. Transport Minister Elena Kavanaugh unveiled the plan at a press conference held at Reyville City Hall, alongside Mayor Thomas Ndiaye. The funding, allocated under the National Infrastructure Renewal Act, will finance repairs to the Kirsten River Bridge and the construction of a new overpass on Route 9. Kavanaugh stated that the Ministry selected Bramwell Engineering, a construction firm headquartered in Port Alden, to lead the project after a competitive bidding process. Bramwell Engineering is a subsidiary of Halloway Industries, a conglomerate based in the capital, Verrance. Work is scheduled to begin on 1 April 2024 and conclude by December 2025. Mayor Ndiaye praised the initiative, noting that the Kirsten River Bridge has been closed to heavy vehicles since a partial collapse in November 2022 injured three pedestrians. "This investment will protect commuters and support nearly 1,200 construction jobs," Kavanaugh said. The Ministry also confirmed that inspectors from the Bureau of Public Works will conduct quarterly safety audits throughout construction. Opposition lawmaker Priya Chandrasekaran criticized the timeline as overly optimistic, calling for an independent review before funds are disbursed. The Ministry expects final approval from Parliament by 20 March 2024.

The Ohio Department of Transportation (ODOT) announced on March 11, 2024 that it will begin a $47 million reconstruction of Interstate 70 between Springfield and Columbus, Ohio, starting April 1, 2024. Director Jack Marchbanks said the project, awarded to contractor Kokosing Construction Company, will replace 6.2 miles of aging pavement and repair three bridges over the Mad River. "This investment will reduce congestion and improve safety for the roughly 58,000 vehicles that travel this corridor daily," Marchbanks said during a press briefing at the ODOT District 7 office in Sidney, Ohio. Funding includes $32 million from the Ohio Department of Transportation's capital budget and $15 million from the federal Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, administered by the Federal Highway Administration. Governor Mike DeWine praised the plan, noting that similar work completed last year on Interstate 75 near Dayton reduced crash rates by 18 percent. Construction is expected to conclude by November 30, 2025, though officials cautioned that winter weather could delay the timeline by up to six weeks. Local business owner Elena Ruiz, who operates a diner near the Route 4 interchange, expressed concern that lane closures could hurt sales during the busiest summer months. ODOT will hold a public forum on March 25, 2024 at Springfield City Hall to address resident questions and provide updated detour maps ahead of the closures.

AUSTIN, Texas -- Meridian Robotics Inc. announced on June 4, 2024 that it has acquired Voltera Dynamics, a Denver-based manufacturer of industrial battery packs, for 92 million dollars in cash and stock. The deal, finalized at Meridian's headquarters in Austin, Texas, is expected to close by August 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Meridian Robotics, founded in 2016 by chief executive officer Diane Okafor, designs autonomous warehouse robots used by logistics companies across North America. Voltera Dynamics, led by founder Marcus Lindqvist, supplies lithium-ion battery modules to several robotics firms, including Meridian's competitor, Foreman Automation.

"This acquisition strengthens our supply chain and lets us control battery production in-house," said Diane Okafor during a press conference held at the Austin facility on Tuesday. Marcus Lindqvist will join Meridian as senior vice president of energy systems, effective July 1, 2024.

Meridian also announced that Rajiv Patel, previously chief operating officer, will step down from his position on June 30, 2024 to pursue an opportunity at a startup in Seattle. The company will promote vice president Elena Torres to chief operating officer, effective July 1, 2024.

Meridian Robotics reported revenue of 340 million dollars in fiscal year 2023, up 18 percent from the prior year. Shares of Meridian, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker MRDN, rose 6 percent following the announcement. The combined company will employ approximately 1,200 workers across facilities in Austin, Denver, and Toronto.

4/ Solstice, founded in 2015 by Priya Nandakumar and her brother Raj Nandakumar, is headquartered in Austin, Texas and competes directly with Kessler Autonomics in the warehouse-robotics space.

CHICAGO, Illinois - Deere & Company announced on Tuesday, March 11, 2025, that it has completed the acquisition of Sparton Precision Ag, a Nebraska-based maker of soil-sensing equipment, for $412 million in cash. The deal, first disclosed in January, gives Deere direct access to Sparton's proprietary soil-mapping technology, which the company plans to integrate into its next-generation tractors within 18 months.

Deere Chief Executive Officer John May said the acquisition strengthens the company's precision-agriculture division at a time when farmers face tighter margins and unpredictable weather patterns linked to climate change. "This is about giving growers tools that make every acre count," May said during a call with analysts from Deere's headquarters in Moline, Illinois.

Sparton Precision Ag, founded in 2016 by engineer Rosalind Farber, employs about 340 people at its facility in Lincoln, Nebraska. Farber will join Deere as Vice President of Soil Analytics, reporting directly to May, effective April 1, 2025. Two of Sparton's co-founders, however, are expected to depart the combined company by June.

Shares of Deere rose 2.3 percent to $402.15 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of rival Caterpillar Inc. dipped slightly. Analyst Priya Nathan of Morgan Stanley called the deal "a smart, if pricey, bet on data-driven farming," noting that competitor CNH Industrial has also been expanding its own precision-ag portfolio. Deere expects the acquisition to be completed and fully integrated by the fourth quarter of 2025.

CHICAGO, Nov. 14 — Meridian Foods Corp., the packaged-snacks maker headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, agreed on Thursday to acquire rival snack producer Prairie Crunch Inc. for $410 million in cash, the companies announced. Under the deal, Meridian will buy all outstanding shares of Prairie Crunch, based in Madison, Wisconsin, with the transaction expected to close by January 2025 pending regulatory approval.

Meridian's chief executive officer, Diane Okafor, said the acquisition would expand the company's presence in the Midwest and add Prairie Crunch's popular Harvest Bites product line to Meridian's portfolio. "This is a natural fit for both organizations," Okafor told reporters during a press conference at Meridian's headquarters. Prairie Crunch founder Walter Hines, who started the company in 1998, will join Meridian's board of directors as part of the agreement.

Analysts at Blackstone Ridge Capital noted that the deal positions Meridian to compete more directly with Fairmont Snacks Group, the current market leader in the Midwest region. Shares of Prairie Crunch, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker PRCR, jumped 18 percent following the announcement, while Meridian's stock slipped 3 percent amid investor concerns over the debt used to finance the purchase.

The boards of both companies have unanimously approved the merger. Meridian said it expects to fund the deal through a combination of $250 million in new debt and existing cash reserves. The company plans to retain all 1,200 Prairie Crunch employees at its Madison manufacturing plant.

Pixelworks Labs, a Portland-based imaging startup founded by former Intel engineer Marcus Delaney, unveiled the Aura Q7 tablet on September 14, 2023, at a press event in San Jose, California. Priced at $649, the Aura Q7 features a 12.4-inch OLED display and a proprietary chip called Helion X1, which Pixelworks Labs says was co-developed with supplier Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company. I have used the Aura Q7 for three weeks, and it is easily the most impressive tablet I have tested this year. Battery life stretched to 14 hours during continuous video playback, beating the Apple iPad Air by roughly 3 hours in my tests. The 8-megapixel front camera handles video calls well, and the stylus, sold separately for $79, offers negligible lag. My only complaint is software: the custom interface, called AuraOS, occasionally freezes when switching between more than 6 open apps. Pixelworks Labs' chief executive officer, Delaney, told reporters on September 15 that a software patch would arrive by October 2023. Competitor Samsung Electronics, headquartered in Suwon, South Korea, declined to comment on the Aura Q7's pricing strategy. Still, at $649, the Aura Q7 undercuts the $799 Galaxy Tab S9 while matching much of its performance. For students and casual creatives on a budget, this is one of the strongest values in tablets released in 2023. I recommend it without hesitation.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- Nov 14, 2023 -- Verdant Biosciences Inc. announced today that it has acquired Solara Diagnostics LLC, a privately held maker of rapid point-of-care testing devices, for $84 million in cash. The transaction, expected to close by Dec 1, 2023, will make Solara Diagnostics a wholly owned subsidiary of Verdant Biosciences and expand the company's footprint in infectious disease screening.

Under the agreement, Verdant Biosciences will pay Solara Diagnostics shareholders $84 million, with an additional $12 million in milestone payments tied to regulatory approval of the SolaraScan device by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. SolaraScan, a handheld diagnostic tool capable of detecting influenza and respiratory syncytial virus within 15 minutes, has already received clearance in the European Union.

"This acquisition strengthens our diagnostics portfolio and accelerates our path into point-of-care testing," said Marcus Aldridge, Chief Executive Officer of Verdant Biosciences. Aldridge, who joined the company in 2019, will oversee integration efforts alongside Solara Diagnostics founder Priya Nandakumar, who will step down as Chief Executive Officer of Solara Diagnostics but remain as a strategic advisor.

Verdant Biosciences, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs roughly 1,200 people worldwide and reported $410 million in revenue last year. Solara Diagnostics, based in Austin, Texas, was founded in 2016 and has 95 employees. The deal marks Verdant Biosciences' third acquisition since 2021, following its purchase of NovaGene Labs for $30 million in 2022.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday, 14 May 2024 that Singapore will invest 480 million Singapore dollars to upgrade the Woodlands Checkpoint, the nation's busiest land border crossing with Malaysia. Speaking at a press conference in Singapore, Transport Minister Chee Hong Tat said the project, called the Woodlands Integrated Checkpoint, will expand vehicle lanes by 40 percent and reduce clearance times by 2026. The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority, a statutory board under the Ministry of Home Affairs, will oversee construction, which is expected to begin in September 2024 and finish within three years. Chee Hong Tat noted that daily crossings at Woodlands Checkpoint have risen to roughly 300,000 travelers, up from 250,000 before the COVID-19 pandemic. He added that the government will also allocate 60 million Singapore dollars to hire an additional 500 officers over the next two years to staff the expanded facility. The announcement follows a bilateral meeting last week in Kuala Lumpur between Chee Hong Tat and Malaysia's Transport Minister Anthony Loke, where both sides agreed to synchronize customs clearance systems by 2025. Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, who attended the Singapore briefing, said the upgrade reflects Singapore's commitment to strengthening ties with Malaysia amid growing cross-border trade, which reached 130 billion Singapore dollars in 2023. Construction contracts will be awarded through a public tender managed by the Building and Construction Authority starting in July 2024.

Boston, MA -- April 9, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolzurabin, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Verinta Therapeutics, for treatment of relapsing multiple sclerosis. The study, led by Dr. Naomi Elsworth, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and March 2023. Participants received either 300 milligrams of tolzurabin administered intravenously every eight weeks or a placebo. After 52 weeks, the treatment group showed a 47 percent reduction in annualized relapse rate compared to placebo, and MRI scans revealed 62 percent fewer new lesions. Dr. Elsworth presented the findings at the American Academy of Neurology meeting in Denver on April 8, 2024. "These results suggest tolzurabin could become a first-line option for patients who fail interferon-based therapies," she said. Verinta Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by former Biogen executive Marcus Whitfield, plans to file for FDA approval by early 2025 and has already secured $85 million in Series C funding led by Andover Capital Partners to support a planned phase 3 trial involving 600 patients. Common adverse events included mild headache and injection-site reactions, reported by 18 percent of participants; no serious cardiac or hepatic toxicity was observed. The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov and funded in part by a $4.2 million grant from the National Multiple Sclerosis Society. Independent experts, including Dr. Rajiv Chandra of the Mayo Clinic, called the data "encouraging but preliminary," noting that longer-term safety data will be essential before broader adoption.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., March 4, 2024 - Vantix Therapeutics, Inc. announced today that it has acquired Norrin Biosciences Ltd., a Dublin-based biotechnology firm specializing in RNA-targeted therapies, for approximately 340 million dollars in cash and stock. The deal, finalized on February 29, 2024, gives Vantix full rights to Norrin's lead compound, VX-771, currently in Phase II trials for treating cystic fibrosis.

Under the terms of the agreement, Norrin shareholders will receive 12 dollars per share, representing a 45 percent premium over the company's closing price on the Dublin Stock Exchange last month. The transaction is expected to close by the end of the second quarter, pending regulatory approval from the European Commission.

"This acquisition strengthens our pipeline and accelerates our entry into respiratory genetic disease markets," said Dr. Elena Marsh, Chief Executive Officer of Vantix Therapeutics. Marsh, who joined Vantix in 2019, will oversee the integration alongside Norrin's outgoing CEO, Patrick Doyle, who will step down from his position on April 15, 2024.

Vantix, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs roughly 1,200 people across the United States and Europe. The company was founded in 2011 by Dr. Elena Marsh and Dr. Samuel Owusu, who now serves as Chief Scientific Officer. Norrin Biosciences, founded in 2015, employs 210 researchers at its facility in Dublin, Ireland.

Shares of Vantix rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, while analysts at Concord Capital Partners called the deal "a smart bet on next-generation gene therapy."

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City edged past Everton 2-1 at Etihad Stadium on Saturday, with substitute Julian Alvarez scoring the decisive goal in the 84th minute. The victory extended City's unbeaten run in the Premier League to nine matches and kept manager Pep Guardiola's side atop the table with 22 points after nine games.

Erling Haaland opened the scoring for City in the 23rd minute, converting a Kevin De Bruyne cross with a close-range header. Everton responded eleven minutes later when Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalized from the penalty spot after James Tarkowski was fouled in the box. The score remained level until Alvarez's late strike, which came after a swift counterattack started by De Bruyne near midfield.

A crowd of 53,112 attended the match, one of the largest at Etihad Stadium this season. Guardiola praised his squad's composure afterward, telling reporters, "We showed patience against a well-organized Everton team, and Julian's finish was exactly what we needed."

Everton manager Sean Dyche, whose side dropped to 15th place with 8 points, said the result was harsh given his team's second-half performance. The Toffees' next fixture is against Newcastle United on October 21, while City will travel to Estadio do Dragao to face FC Porto in the UEFA Champions League on October 17.

City's win moved them three points clear of second-placed Arsenal, who face Brentford at the Emirates Stadium this weekend.

On March 14, 2024, Judge Patricia Nomura sentenced Darnell Ruiz, 41, to 54 months in state prison after a jury in Oakland convicted him of grand theft and embezzlement from his former employer, Cascade Freight Logistics Inc. Prosecutor Ellen Marsh of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Ruiz, who worked as a Senior Accounts Manager at Cascade Freight Logistics from January 2019 until his termination in August 2023, diverted $312,000 in client payments into a shell account registered under the name Bluewater Consulting LLC.

Defense attorney Ramon Castillo told the court his client accepted responsibility and had already repaid $40,000 to the company. Judge Nomura, presiding over Department 12 at the René C. Davidson Courthouse, ordered Ruiz to pay $272,000 in restitution to Cascade Freight Logistics within five years of his release.

The case, People v. Darnell Ruiz, was originally filed on September 22, 2023, after an internal audit by Cascade Freight Logistics uncovered irregular wire transfers dating back to March 2021. Ruiz was arrested on October 3, 2023, by detectives from the Oakland Police Department at his residence in San Leandro. He was arraigned on October 17, 2023, and pleaded not guilty before later changing his plea in February 2024.

Cascade Freight Logistics, headquartered in Emeryville, California, issued a statement thanking the Alameda County DA's office and confirmed it has since implemented new financial controls across its 14 regional offices.

DENVER, Colorado - Trailhead Energy Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Basin Ridge Resources LLC, a privately held natural gas producer based in Midland, Texas, for $412 million in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing at Trailhead's headquarters, marks the company's largest acquisition since its founding in 2009 by CEO Marcus Aldridge.

Under the terms of the agreement, Trailhead will pay $275 million in cash and issue 4.8 million shares of common stock to Basin Ridge's owners, including founder Elena Vasquez, who will join Trailhead's board as a non-executive director starting December 1. Analysts at Fairview Capital Partners estimated the transaction values Basin Ridge at roughly 6.5 times projected 2025 earnings.

"This acquisition strengthens our position in the Permian Basin and adds nearly 40,000 net acres to our portfolio," Aldridge said during the briefing, which was attended by reporters from Reuters and Bloomberg.

Trailhead shares rose 7.3 percent to $58.20 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume surged to 2.1 million shares, well above the daily average of 640,000. The company expects the acquisition to close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

Separately, Trailhead said longtime Chief Financial Officer Daniel Okafor will step down on November 30 to pursue other opportunities, with controller Sarah Lindqvist appointed as interim CFO effective December 1.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- Nov 14, 2023 -- Arclight Biotherapeutics, Inc. announced today that it has acquired Verdant Genomics Corp., a privately held gene-editing company based in Boulder, Colorado, for $340 million in cash and stock. The transaction, finalized on Nov 13, 2023, expands Arclight's pipeline into inherited retinal diseases, including Leber congenital amaurosis.

Under the terms of the deal, Verdant Genomics shareholders will receive $12.50 per share, representing a 28% premium over the company's last closing price. The acquisition was approved unanimously by both boards of directors.

"This acquisition strengthens our position in precision gene therapy," said Dr. Priya Nandakumar, Chief Executive Officer of Arclight Biotherapeutics. "Verdant's CRISPR-based platform, VerdiEdit, complements our existing programs and accelerates our timeline toward a 2026 regulatory filing."

Verdant Genomics was founded in 2017 by Dr. Marcus Feldt in Boulder, Colorado, and has since grown to 85 employees. Dr. Feldt will join Arclight as Senior Vice President of Gene Therapy Research, effective Dec 1, 2023.

Arclight Biotherapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs approximately 610 people and is listed on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol ARCB. The company was founded in 2011 by Dr. Priya Nandakumar and Dr. Samuel Okafor.

The deal is expected to close by Jan 15, 2024, pending customary regulatory approvals. J.P. Morgan Securities LLC acted as financial advisor to Arclight, while Centerview Partners advised Verdant Genomics.

input: The Ohio Department of Transportation (ODOT) announced on Tuesday that it will invest $42 million to repair the Fremont Bridge along Interstate 90 near Sandusky, Ohio, after inspectors found structural cracks in March. Director Marcus Whitfield said the project, awarded to contractor Blake Construction Group, will begin on May 6, 2024 and is expected to finish by November 2025. "This bridge carries more than 38,000 vehicles daily, and safety cannot wait," Whitfield said during a press briefing at ODOT's Columbus headquarters. The funding includes $30 million from the Federal Highway Administration and $12 million from state transportation bonds. Governor Elena Torres praised the plan, noting that similar repairs on the Maumee River Bridge in Toledo were completed under budget in 2022. Blake Construction Group, headquartered in Akron, previously worked with ODOT on the Interstate 71 resurfacing project completed in 2019. ODOT spokesperson Rita Alvarado said lane closures will begin at 9:00 p.m. on May 6 and traffic will be rerouted through State Route 2. Local business owners, including Diane Kessler of Sandusky Harbor Seafood, expressed concern about reduced customer access during construction. ODOT has scheduled a public forum for April 18, 2024 at Sandusky City Hall to address community questions. Whitfield added that a follow-up inspection report will be released by the Ohio Bureau of Bridge Engineering in December 2025 to confirm the repairs meet federal safety standards.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday, June 11, 2024, that it will invest 480 million euros to modernize rail infrastructure across the Occitanie region of France. Minister Élodie Fabron unveiled the plan at a press conference in Toulouse, stating that the funds will replace aging signal systems on the Toulouse-Montauban corridor by December 2026. The initiative, named Rail Renouveau, will be overseen by the state rail operator SNCF, whose director general, Jean-Pierre Farandou, confirmed that construction crews will begin work near Montauban station on September 2, 2024. Fabron noted that the project follows a 2023 audit that found signal failures caused 14 percent of regional delays last year. Local officials in Toulouse welcomed the announcement, though the regional council president, Carole Delga, urged the ministry to extend similar funding to the Occitanie-Pyrénées line. The Ministry also confirmed that SNCF will purchase 22 new regional trainsets from Alstom, headquartered in Saint-Ouen, for approximately 310 million euros, with deliveries expected to begin in early 2027. Alstom's chief executive, Henri Poupart-Lafarge, said the contract would support roughly 900 jobs at the company's Reichshoffen plant. Opposition lawmaker Julien Roux criticized the timeline as too slow, arguing that commuters in Montauban have already endured three years of delays. The Ministry of Transport said further details on the Occitanie-Pyrénées line would be published before the end of 2024.

Fjord & Pine Outfitters is now shipping the Rambler 45L Trail Pack, a rugged travel backpack designed for multi-day treks. Priced at $189.00 and available in Slate Gray or Moss Green, the Rambler 45L launched on September 12, 2024 and is manufactured in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Each pack uses 420-denier ripstop nylon sourced from Toray Industries and features a hip belt rated to carry loads up to 25 kilograms. Fjord & Pine Outfitters, headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, was founded in 2016 by former REI buyer Kristin Ahlgren, who now serves as the company's Chief Product Officer. The Rambler 45L has already drawn praise from Backpacker Monthly, which awarded it the Editors' Choice Award at the Outdoor Retailer Summer Market in Denver, Colorado on June 18, 2024. Competing directly with Osprey Packs and Gregory Mountain Products, the Rambler line aims to undercut rivals by roughly 15 percent on price while matching durability. Customers who purchase before October 31, 2024 receive a free 2-liter hydration bladder, a $22.00 value. The pack ships in a 100% recycled cardboard box and includes a lifetime warranty covering defects in materials and workmanship. Fjord & Pine Outfitters reports that over 8,000 units sold in the first month alone, according to spokesperson Daniel Ortiz. Reviewers on the company's website give the Rambler 45L an average rating of 4.7 out of 5 stars across 312 reviews. The bag weighs 1.9 kilograms empty and folds flat for storage, making it a favorite among gear reviewers at OutsideXtra magazine.

CHICAGO, Nov. 14 -- Deere & Company announced Tuesday that it has acquired AgriSense Technologies, a Champaign, Illinois-based startup specializing in soil-moisture sensors, for $340 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by January 15, 2025, marks Deere's third acquisition this year as the farm-equipment giant pushes deeper into precision agriculture. AgriSense, founded in 2016 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, employs roughly 120 people and reported $28 million in revenue last year. Nandakumar will join Deere as Vice President of Digital Agriculture, reporting directly to Chief Executive Officer John May. "This is a natural extension of our strategy to give farmers real-time data," May said during a press call from Deere's headquarters in Moline, Illinois. Shares of Deere rose 2.4 percent to $412.18 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement. Analyst Mark Feldstein of Baird Equity Research called the acquisition "a smart, if pricey, bet on the future of farming," noting that competitor Caterpillar has also been expanding its agricultural technology portfolio. Deere financed the purchase through existing cash reserves and a $150 million short-term loan from JPMorgan Chase. The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which is expected to review the deal over the next 60 days. Deere's stock has climbed nearly 18 percent since the start of the fiscal year, buoyed by strong demand for autonomous tractors in North America and Brazil.

Pixel Tab 3, Google's new tablet unveiled on March 14, 2024, in Mountain View, California, finally arrived on store shelves last week, and after nine days of testing I have mixed feelings. Priced at $649 for the 128GB Wi-Fi model, the device pairs a 10.9-inch OLED screen with the Tensor G4 chip, the same silicon found in the Pixel 9 phone. Sundar Pichai, chief executive of Google's parent company Alphabet Inc., called it "the most ambitious tablet we have ever built" during the launch event at the Shoreline Amphitheatre. In practice, the screen is genuinely gorgeous, and battery life stretched to roughly 11 hours of video playback in my trials. Where it stumbles is software: several third-party apps, including Slack and Spotify, still render in a stretched phone layout rather than a proper tablet interface. Google says a fix is coming with the Android 15 update expected in September 2024. Samsung, the company's chief rival in the tablet market with its Galaxy Tab S9 line, still holds an edge in app optimization, according to analyst Priya Ramaswamy of Gartner. I also tested the optional $129 keyboard case, which felt flimsy after just two weeks of daily use. For $649, buyers are getting excellent hardware bundled with unfinished software. I recommend waiting for the September update before committing, unless you already live inside Google's ecosystem.

OTTAWA, October 14, 2024 - The Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Canada today announced a $420 million initiative to accelerate the phase-out of coal-fired power plants across Alberta and Saskatchewan by 2030. Minister Elena Whitfield unveiled the program, called the Clean Grid Transition Fund, during a press conference at the Sir John A. Macdonald Building. "This funding will help TransAlta Corporation and SaskPower retrain approximately 3,200 workers and modernize regional grids," Whitfield said. Pixelworks Labs, a hardware startup based in Portland, Oregon, unveiled the Aria S1 tablet on June 4, 2024, promising creative professionals a lighter alternative to the Apple iPad Pro. Founder and CEO Miriam Okafor demonstrated the device at a press event in San Jose, California, showing off its 12.9-inch micro-LED display and a claimed 14-hour battery life. The Aria S1 will retail for $899 when it ships on July 15, 2024, undercutting the iPad Pro by roughly $300.

I spent eight days testing a review unit that Pixelworks Labs shipped to me from its Portland facility. The screen is genuinely stunning, and the stylus latency, measured at 9 milliseconds, edges out Apple's offering. However, the software ecosystem remains thin; only 40 apps in the Aria Store are currently optimized for the larger canvas, and Adobe has not yet committed to a native Photoshop build.

Battery life fell short of the advertised figure, lasting closer to 10 hours under my mixed workload. Pixelworks Labs says a firmware update, expected in August 2024, will improve power efficiency by 15 percent. The company, which employs about 120 people, also confirmed it raised $45 million in a Series C round led by Meridian Ventures in March 2024.

For illustrators and photographers frustrated with Apple's walled garden, the Aria S1 is a compelling, if imperfect, first attempt. I'd wait for the August firmware patch before recommending it for professional use, but the hardware foundation here is unusually strong for a first-generation product.

input: Marguerite Okonjo-Lévy (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-French microbiologist known for pioneering work on cholera vaccine development. She earned her doctorate in molecular biology from the University of Lyon in 1984 and joined the Institut Pasteur in Paris the following year as a research fellow. In 1991 she was appointed Head of the Bacteriology Division at Institut Pasteur, a position she held for over a decade. Her laboratory identified a mutation in Vibrio cholerae that informed the design of an oral vaccine later licensed by Sanofi Pasteur. In 2003 she left Institut Pasteur to become Director of Research at the World Health Organization office in Geneva, Switzerland, overseeing outbreak-response programs across sub-Saharan Africa. She led emergency teams during the 2008 cholera outbreak in Harare, Zimbabwe, coordinating with local health ministries to distribute over 2 million doses of vaccine within three months. Okonjo-Lévy married fellow scientist Daniel Lévy in 1986; their daughter, Amina Lévy, later became an epidemiologist at Johns Hopkins University. In 2015 the World Health Assembly awarded her the Lasker Prize in Geneva for her contributions to global public health. She retired from the WHO in 2019 and now serves on the advisory board of Médecins Sans Frontières. Her memoir, "Water and Blood," was published in 2021 by Éditions Gallimard and has sold over 150,000 copies worldwide.

Denver-based food-delivery firm SwiftBite Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired local rival GrubDash for $340 million in a cash-and-stock deal. The transaction, disclosed at a press briefing in Denver, Colorado, values GrubDash at roughly 12 times its projected 2025 revenue. SwiftBite's chief executive, Marcus Whitfield, said the acquisition would expand the company's footprint into Salt Lake City and Boise, where GrubDash currently operates. "This merger strengthens our position against DoorDash and Uber Eats," Whitfield told reporters. GrubDash founder Elena Ruiz, who started the company in 2018, will join SwiftBite's board as a senior advisor beginning November 1. Under the deal terms, SwiftBite will pay $220 million in cash and issue $120 million worth of common stock to GrubDash shareholders. The deal is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners estimate the combined company will process more than 4 million orders per week across 38 cities. Shares of SwiftBite rose 6.3 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, closing at $58.42. GrubDash, which employed about 1,200 people as of March 2024, will retain its Boise office as a regional hub. Whitfield added that no layoffs are currently planned, though he acknowledged some overlapping roles in marketing and logistics departments would be reviewed over the coming quarter. The deal marks SwiftBite's third acquisition since 2021.

His successor has not yet been named. The announcement was made at a joint press conference attended by representatives from the Rotterdam Port Authority and the Dutch Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management. HARTFORD, Conn. — Meridian Aerospace Corp. announced Tuesday that it will acquire Bristow Dynamics Ltd. for $412 million in cash, a deal expected to close by December 15, 2024. The agreement, disclosed at Meridian's headquarters in Hartford, Connecticut, marks the aerospace manufacturer's largest purchase since its founding in 1998 by engineer Diane Kessler.

Under the terms outlined by Meridian CEO Rajiv Patel, Bristow Dynamics, a British maker of turbine components based in Bristol, England, will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary. Patel said the acquisition strengthens Meridian's supply chain for its regional jet program, the Meridian Falcon 200, and reduces reliance on external suppliers.

"This is about controlling our own destiny," Patel told reporters during a press conference on November 19, 2024. "Bristow's turbine technology fills a critical gap."

Bristow Dynamics was founded in 1987 by British engineer Nigel Ashford, who stepped down as chief executive in 2021. Current Bristow CEO Helen Marsh will join Meridian's executive board as part of the transition, effective January 6, 2025.

Shares of Meridian Aerospace rose 6.4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while analysts at Fenwick Capital Partners estimated the deal could add $75 million in annual revenue by 2026. The transaction still requires approval from British regulators and is expected to face review under the UK's National Security and Investment Act.

Meridian employs roughly 14,000 workers across facilities in Hartford, Toulouse, and Singapore.

DETROIT, Mich. — Automaker Ferrand Motors announced Tuesday it will acquire electric vehicle startup Voltrix Inc. for $2.3 billion, marking one of the largest deals in the sector this year. The agreement was signed at Ferrand's headquarters in Detroit and is expected to close by March 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval.

Ferrand Motors CEO Denise Halbrook said the acquisition of Voltrix, founded in 2018 by engineer Priya Raman, will accelerate production of the company's flagship electric sedan, the Voltrix Aria. "This is about combining Ferrand's manufacturing scale with Voltrix's battery technology," Halbrook said during a press conference attended by reporters from Reuters and Bloomberg.

Raman, who will remain as Chief Technology Officer under the new arrangement, called the deal a "natural next step" for the six-year-old company, which is based in Austin, Texas. Voltrix currently employs 1,200 workers and operates a battery plant in Nevada.

Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimate the merger could boost Ferrand's annual revenue by 18 percent within two years. Shares of Ferrand Motors rose 6.4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of competitor Bolt Dynamics fell 3.1 percent.

The deal still requires clearance from the Federal Trade Commission. If approved, Voltrix will operate as a subsidiary of Ferrand Motors while retaining its Austin headquarters, the companies said.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT PRESS STATEMENT
Ottawa, Ontario — March 14, 2024

The Ministry of Transport announced today that Minister Andrea Fontaine will allocate $85 million in federal funding to upgrade the Trans-Canada Highway between Regina and Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan. The project, formally named the Prairie Corridor Renewal Initiative, is expected to begin construction on May 6, 2024 and conclude by November 2026.

Speaking at a press briefing in Regina, Minister Fontaine stated, "This investment reflects our government's commitment to safer roads and stronger supply chains across the Prairies." The funding will be transferred to the Saskatchewan Ministry of Highways in three installments, with the first payment of $28 million scheduled for April 2024.

The announcement follows a review conducted by Deputy Minister Robert Chan, who joined the Ministry of Transport in January 2023 after leaving his post at Bombardier Inc. Chan noted that roughly 14 percent of freight accidents on the corridor in 2023 were linked to deteriorating pavement conditions.

Opposition critic Marie-Claude Tremblay, a Member of Parliament representing Saskatoon West, welcomed the funding but questioned why similar investment had not been directed toward Highway 16 near Prince Albert. The Ministry responded that a separate $40 million package for Highway 16 will be considered in the 2025 federal budget.

Construction will be carried out by PCL Constructors Canada Inc., which was awarded the contract following a competitive bidding process completed on February 20, 2024.

The Ontario Ministry of Transportation announced on May 14, 2024 that it will invest $220 million to widen Highway 401 between Milton and Mississauga, a project expected to reduce commute times by 18 percent once completed. Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria, speaking at a press briefing in Toronto, said construction will begin on August 1, 2024 and continue through late 2027. The contract was awarded to Aecon Group Inc., headquartered in Toronto, following a competitive bidding process that also included EllisDon Corporation. Sarkaria noted that the expansion forms part of the province's broader Building Ontario Plan, a policy framework first introduced in 2022 to modernize highway infrastructure across Ontario. Deputy Minister Renu Kulendran added that the ministry expects to create approximately 3,500 construction jobs over the next three years. Local officials, including Milton Mayor Gordon Krantz, welcomed the funding, noting that congestion on the 401 corridor has worsened since 2019. The ministry will hold a public consultation session in Mississauga on June 10, 2024 to gather feedback from residents and business owners. Environmental groups, however, have raised concerns about increased emissions, and a small demonstration of roughly 60 people gathered outside Queen's Park in Toronto on May 15, 2024 to protest the highway widening plan. The ministry stated it remains committed to completing an environmental assessment before construction begins.

Pixelbook Forge 14, Reviewed: Google's Steadiest Chromebook Yet

On March 4, 2024, Google launched the Pixelbook Forge 14 at a small press event in Mountain View, California, pricing the new Chromebook at $999. I have spent three weeks with the review unit supplied by Google, and it is the most polished ChromeOS device I have tested since the original Pixelbook.

The Forge 14 pairs an Intel Core i5-1340P with 16GB of RAM and a 512GB SSD, and Google claims 11 hours of battery life. In my testing around Austin, Texas, I consistently got 9.5 hours of mixed use, which is respectable for a 14-inch panel. The 2880x1800 OLED display is the standout feature, and it noticeably outperforms the LCD panel on the Acer Chromebook Spin 714, currently the Forge 14's closest competitor.

Sundar Pichai, chief executive officer of Google, mentioned the laptop briefly during a call with analysts on March 6, 2024, noting that Google sold roughly 40,000 units in the first week alone. That is a modest number next to Apple's MacBook lineup, but strong for a Chromebook.

The keyboard deck flexes slightly under pressure, and the 1080p webcam is merely adequate in low light. Software support is promised through 2032, which is eight years longer than most rivals from Lenovo or HP. For students and light productivity users, the Pixelbook Forge 14 is easy to recommend, though $999 is a steep ask when the Spin 714 sells for $699.

Overall rating: 4 out of 5 stars.

Miriam Kessler (born March 14, 1958, in Winnipeg, Canada) is a Canadian-American biochemist known for her contributions to enzyme engineering. After earning a doctorate from the University of Toronto in 1984, she moved to the United States to join Genentech as a Research Scientist in 1986. In 1993 she left Genentech to co-found Halcyon Biosciences with her longtime collaborator Dr. Owen Ferris, establishing the company's headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Under her leadership as Chief Scientific Officer, Halcyon Biosciences developed a widely used industrial enzyme called Zymuline, produced by Halcyon Biosciences and licensed to agricultural firms across Europe.

In 2002, Kessler was elected to the National Academy of Sciences, and in 2007 she received the Wolf Prize in Chemistry from the Wolf Foundation in Jerusalem. She stepped down as Chief Scientific Officer of Halcyon Biosciences in December 2015, remaining on the board of directors. In 2018, Novartis acquired Halcyon Biosciences for 640 million dollars, a deal announced in Basel, Switzerland.

Kessler is married to physicist Daniel Ferris and has one daughter, Elena Ferris, born in 1990 in Boston. She currently holds an honorary professorship at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and continues to publish research on protein folding. Kessler is a member of the American Chemical Society and has authored more than 120 peer-reviewed papers over her four-decade career.

CHICAGO, Illinois -- Midwest Rail Corp., a freight logistics company headquartered in Chicago, announced Tuesday that it has acquired Prairie Line Transport Inc. for $340 million in cash. The deal, unveiled at a press conference at Midwest Rail's downtown headquarters, was signed by CEO Angela Torres and Prairie Line founder Robert Kessler.

Under the agreement, Prairie Line Transport, based in Springfield, Illinois, will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Midwest Rail Corp. Torres said the acquisition will add 1,200 employees and 85 locomotives to Midwest Rail's fleet. "This partnership positions us as a top competitor to Union Pacific in the regional freight market," Torres told reporters.

Kessler, who founded Prairie Line Transport in 1998, will step down as chief executive officer effective November 15, 2024, and will be replaced by longtime Midwest Rail executive David Chen, who will start as president of the subsidiary that same day.

The transaction, first reported by the Chicago Tribune, still requires approval from the Surface Transportation Board, a federal regulatory agency. Analysts at Morningstar estimate the combined company could generate $2.1 billion in annual revenue by 2026.

Shares of Midwest Rail Corp. rose 4.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement. The company employs roughly 9,000 workers across twelve states.

Prosecutor Michael Torrance of the Maricopa County Attorney's Office argued that Ogilvie broke into unit 214 on the night of January 12, 2024, and removed a 2019 Ford F-150 valued at approximately $28,500, later sold to an unlicensed buyer in Tucson for $9,000 cash.

Defense attorney Renata Blackwood, representing Ogilvie, requested leniency, citing her client's cooperation with detectives from the Chandler Police Department, who arrested him on February 3, 2024, at a motel on Alma School Road. Judge Nunez, addressing the courtroom, stated that the sentence reflected both the value of the stolen property and Ogilvie's two prior convictions in Pima County. The Ford F-150 has since been recovered and returned to its owner, Sonoran Ridge Storage client Louis Feldman. Ogilvie will be eligible for parole review in 2027, according to court records filed by the Arizona Department of Corrections.

SUPERIOR COURT OF ALAMEDA COUNTY, CALIFORNIA — On March 14, 2024, Judge Renata Solis sentenced Marcus Fell, 41, to 46 months in federal prison after a jury in Oakland convicted him of wire fraud and embezzlement connected to his former role as Chief Financial Officer of Bramwell Logistics Inc., a freight brokerage headquartered in San Leandro, California. Prosecutor Dana Okafor, representing the Alameda County District Attorney's Office, argued that Fell diverted $2.3 million from company accounts between January 2019 and October 2022 to fund personal real estate purchases in Reno, Nevada. Defense attorney Priya Chandrasekaran told the court her client accepted responsibility and had already repaid $410,000 to Bramwell Logistics Inc. Judge Solis, who presided over the three-week trial held at the René C. Davidson Courthouse, ordered Fell to pay $1.9 million in restitution, payable in installments beginning May 1, 2024. Bramwell Logistics Inc. was acquired by Union Pacific Freightways in 2023, and its current chief executive, Harlan Voss, issued a statement saying the company had strengthened internal audit controls since discovering the fraud in November 2022. Fell was arrested by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation on December 8, 2022, at his home in Piedmont, California, on charges of wire fraud and embezzlement. He is scheduled to begin serving his sentence at a federal facility on April 30, 2024. The case, formally titled United States v. Marcus Fell, drew attention from local business groups concerned about oversight failures at mid-sized logistics firms across Northern California.

BOSTON, MA -- May 14, 2024 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported promising results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovamirab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cascade Therapeutics, in patients with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti, enrolled 214 adults across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2022 and September 2023. Participants received either 300 milligrams of tovamirab or placebo every four weeks for 24 weeks. According to results published in The New England Journal of Medicine, 47 percent of patients receiving tovamirab achieved clinical remission at week 24, compared with 19 percent in the placebo group, a statistically significant difference (p<0.001). Serious adverse events occurred in 6 percent of the treatment arm, including two cases of severe infection requiring hospitalization in Toronto. Dr. Marchetti presented the findings at the Digestive Disease Week conference in Washington, D.C. on May 12, 2024. Cascade Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, stated it plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. The company's chief executive officer, Raj Patel, said the data represent "a meaningful step forward" for patients who have not responded to existing therapies such as infliximab. Cascade Therapeutics was founded in 2016 and is a subsidiary of Meridian Biosciences, based in Basel, Switzerland. Analysts at Jefferies estimate peak annual sales of tovamirab could reach $1.8 billion if approved. The company's shares rose 11 percent following the announcement.

input: MADRID, June 14 — Real Sociedad striker Mikel Oyarzabal scored twice as Spain defeated Croatia 3-1 on Friday night in a friendly at the Estadio Santiago Bernabéu, boosting confidence ahead of the team's opening match at the 2026 World Cup. Croatia's lone response came from forward Ante Budimir in the 54th minute. BOSTON, MA -- March 14, 2024 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating apixafenib, an investigational chemical compound designed to inhibit tumor angiogenesis in patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between January 2022 and September 2023. Findings, published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, showed a median progression-free survival of 8.4 months among patients receiving apixafenib combined with gemcitabine, compared to 5.1 months in the control group receiving gemcitabine alone. Approximately 62 percent of treated patients experienced tumor shrinkage of at least 30 percent, while grade 3 adverse events, primarily neutropenia, occurred in 18 percent of participants. Dr. Marchetti presented the data at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago on June 2, 2024, stating that the results "represent a meaningful step forward for a disease with historically poor outcomes." The trial was funded by a $24 million grant from the National Cancer Institute and co-sponsored by Verdant Biosciences, a biotechnology firm headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, which holds the patent for apixafenib. Verdant Biosciences was founded in 2016 by former Pfizer executive Raj Patel, who now serves as the company's Chief Executive Officer. A Phase 3 trial is expected to begin enrollment at Massachusetts General Hospital in early 2025, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimate that, if approved, apixafenib could generate annual revenue exceeding $500 million by 2028, positioning Verdant Biosciences as a competitor to Eli Lilly in the oncology therapeutics market.

input: Charlotte, N.C. -- Piedmont Grain Corp., a regional agribusiness firm, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Wednesday in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of North Carolina, citing $412 million in outstanding debt. Participants received either MGH-2201, an oral sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulator, or placebo over a 96-week period. The research team also disclosed that a related compound, MGH-2202, is now entering preclinical testing for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder. Funding for the trial was provided by the National Multiple Sclerosis Society and the National Institutes of Health under grant R01-NS118732. Co-author Dr. Samuel Okafor, a biostatistician at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, confirmed the results were statistically significant, with a p-value below 0.001.

Ingrid Solberg (born March 14, 1958, in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist and former Director-General of the Institute for Ocean Research in Tromsø. She earned a doctorate in marine ecology from the University of Bergen in 1985 and spent the following decade studying cod migration patterns in the Barents Sea. In 1994 Solberg joined the Institute for Ocean Research as a senior researcher, and on June 3, 2002, she was appointed Director-General, a position she held until her retirement on September 30, 2018.

During her tenure, Solberg founded the Nordic Ocean Monitoring Network in 2005, a consortium that eventually included research bodies from Sweden, Denmark, and Iceland. She also led a controversial 2011 expedition aboard the research vessel Polarstjerne to assess declining herring stocks near Svalbard, publishing findings in the journal Marine Ecology Progress Series. Her 2009 book, Cold Currents, examined the impact of warming Arctic waters on fish populations and won the Nansen Prize, awarded by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, in Oslo in 2010.

Solberg married fellow biologist Erik Halvorsen in 1988; the couple had two children, Marte and Jonas. She currently serves on the advisory board of the World Wildlife Fund Norway and lives in Tromsø. In 2020, she received the Order of St. Olav from King Harald V in recognition of her contributions to marine science.

input: Pixelfold Labs launched the Aurora S2 tablet on September 4, 2024, at a press event in Austin, Texas, and after three weeks of daily use I can say it mostly earns the $649 asking price. The 11-inch OLED display gets impressively bright, hitting 1,200 nits outdoors, and the new Halcyon chipset, built by Pixelfold in partnership with supplier Cascade Semiconductor, handles multitasking without stutter. CEO Renata Voss said at the launch that the Aurora S2 was designed to compete directly with Samsung's Galaxy Tab series and Apple's iPad Pro line. Battery life is the standout feature, lasting roughly 14 hours in my mixed-use testing, well above the 9 hours I typically get from my aging iPad Air. The included stylus, sold separately for $79, feels precise but occasionally lags during fast sketching. Software is where things get shakier: the custom Halo OS, based on a forked version of Android 14, still has rough edges, including a settings menu that crashed twice during setup. Pixelfold, headquartered in San Jose, California, was founded in 2019 by Renata Voss and her brother Mateo Voss, and the company acquired the smaller display maker Lumen Optics in March 2023 to secure OLED supply. For $649, the Aurora S2 is a strong value against pricier rivals, though buyers willing to tolerate a few software bugs will benefit most. I'd recommend it cautiously, with a firm nod toward a promised software update in November 2024 that should address the crashing bug.

Hélène Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Lyon, France) is a French biochemist known for her contributions to enzyme engineering. She earned a doctorate in biochemistry from the University of Strasbourg in 1984 and joined the Institut Pasteur in Paris the following year as a research scientist. In 1991, Marchetti moved to Novartis in Basel, Switzerland, where she led a team investigating industrial enzyme catalysts.

Marchetti is best known for developing a stabilized variant of the enzyme lipase B, marketed under the product name Lipozyme HX, which became widely used in biodiesel production during the early 2000s. In 2003, she founded her own company, BioCatalyx SA, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, to commercialize enzyme technologies for industrial clients. The firm was acquired by DSM Nutritional Products in 2011 for an undisclosed sum reported by Reuters to exceed 40 million Swiss francs.

In 2009, Marchetti received the Novartis Prize for Chemistry, awarded in Basel for her work on biocatalysis. She was elected a member of the French Academy of Sciences in 2015. Marchetti served as Chief Scientific Officer of DSM Nutritional Products from 2011 until her retirement in 2019, after which she stepped down from the position. She currently lives in Annecy, France, and continues to consult for pharmaceutical firms.

Marchetti was married to fellow chemist Bernard Roussel from 1986 until his death in 2020; the couple had one son, Julien Roussel, born in 1990 in Basel.

BOSTON, MA -- May 14, 2024 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tepranexib, an experimental oral inhibitor developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Solvara Therapeutics, for patients with moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The trial, led by Dr. Aisha Whitfield, an associate professor of rheumatology at Harvard Medical School, enrolled 214 participants across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2022 and September 2023. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tepranexib twice daily showed a 62 percent reduction in joint inflammation markers after 24 weeks, compared to 28 percent in the placebo group, according to findings published in The Lancet Rheumatology. Dr. Whitfield presented the data on May 13, 2024, at the American College of Rheumatology's regional meeting in Boston. "These results suggest tepranexib could offer a meaningful alternative to existing biologics such as adalimumab," she said during the presentation. Solvara Therapeutics, founded in 2018 by immunologist Dr. Marcus Lindqvist, plans to begin a Phase 3 trial in early 2025 pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The company's shares, traded privately, attracted a $45 million investment from venture capital firm Northbridge Capital Partners in April 2024 to fund the upcoming trial phase. Common side effects reported included mild headache and nausea, while three patients discontinued treatment due to elevated liver enzymes. No cases of serious infection were reported during the study period. Dr. Whitfield noted that longer-term safety data would be critical before regulatory submission, expected in late 2025.

BOSTON, Feb 14, 2024 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported today that a Phase 2 clinical trial of the investigational compound Nexavirin-B showed a 42 percent reduction in hospitalization rates among patients with severe influenza A. The randomized, double-blind study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, enrolled 318 adults across seven sites in the United States between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received either Nexavirin-B or placebo within 48 hours of symptom onset. Results, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases, indicated that patients treated with Nexavirin-B experienced a median symptom duration of 4.1 days compared to 6.8 days in the placebo group. Dr. Vasquez, an infectious disease specialist affiliated with Harvard Medical School, presented the findings on February 13, 2024, at a conference organized by the American Society for Microbiology in Chicago. "This represents the most promising advance against influenza A we have seen in a decade," Vasquez said during her presentation. Meridian's chief executive, Robert Chen, announced that the company plans to file for FDA approval by the fourth quarter of 2024. Two patients in the treatment arm experienced mild allergic reactions, but no serious adverse events were reported. The randomized, double-blind study enrolled 214 adults across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023. Dr. Rafael Ostrowski, chief medical officer of Beacon Hill Therapeutics, presented the findings at the American Academy of Dermatology annual meeting in San Diego, California. At week 16, 68% of patients receiving BHT-221 achieved a 90% reduction in Psoriasis Area and Severity Index score, compared with 12% in the placebo group (p<0.001). The most common adverse event was mild nasopharyngitis, reported in 9% of treated patients; no cases of serious infection or malignancy were observed. Dr. Ostrowski noted that BHT-221 was well tolerated and could offer a needle-free alternative to injectable biologics such as secukinumab. Beacon Hill Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, plans to initiate a Phase 3 program in early 2025 pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The company was founded in 2018 by Dr. Elena Marsh and is backed by venture funding from Charles River Ventures. Shares of Beacon Hill Therapeutics rose 22% following the announcement. Novartis, a competitor developing similar IL-17 therapies, declined to comment. The full data set will be published in The New England Journal of Medicine later this year.

BOSTON, MA -- April 9, 2024 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tirzomab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cascade Biotherapeutics, for the treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. The 24-week study, led by Dr. Elena Voss, enrolled 312 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany. Participants received either 150 milligrams of tirzomab administered subcutaneously every four weeks or a placebo. According to findings published in The Lancet Dermatology, 68 percent of patients receiving tirzomab achieved at least a 90 percent reduction in psoriasis severity, compared with 12 percent in the placebo group. Dr. Voss presented the data on April 8, 2024, at the American Academy of Dermatology conference in Chicago. "These results suggest tirzomab could become a first-line option for patients who have failed traditional therapies," she said. The most common adverse events were mild upper respiratory infections, reported in 9 percent of participants; no cases of tuberculosis reactivation were observed. Cascade Biotherapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, plans to begin a Phase 3 trial in early 2025 and has requested a meeting with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to discuss an accelerated approval pathway. The company was founded in 2016 by former Genentech scientist Marcus Chen and has raised $310 million in venture funding to date. Delaney was arrested by officers of the Phoenix Police Department on August 6, 2023, two days after the robbery, following a tip from a confidential informant. He was formally indicted on September 15, 2023, on two felony counts. During the trial, which began on February 20, 2024, defense attorney Harold Krum contended that Ibarra could not reliably identify his client, but the jury deliberated for only four hours before returning a guilty verdict on March 5, 2024.

Judge Owens, presiding at the Maricopa County Superior Courthouse, ordered Delaney to pay $1,200 in restitution to Ibarra in addition to the prison term. Delaney's attorney has indicated plans to appeal the sentence to the Arizona Court of Appeals within thirty days.

input: Boston, MA — October 14, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tavuprolib, an experimental oral compound developed by Northbridge Therapeutics for patients with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti, enrolled 214 participants across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2021 and July 2022. Results, published in The New England Journal of Medicine, showed that 47 percent of patients receiving tavuprolib achieved clinical remission at week 12, compared with 19 percent in the placebo group. The most common adverse event was mild headache, reported in 9 percent of the treatment arm. Dr. Marchetti presented the findings at the American College of Gastroenterology annual meeting in Vancouver on October 13, 2023. Northbridge Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, said it plans to file for FDA approval in early 2024 and expects a decision by the fourth quarter of that year. The company, founded in 2015 by biochemist Dr. Raj Patel, previously partnered with Sanofi on an unrelated diabetes program before that collaboration ended in 2020. Shares of Northbridge rose 22 percent following the announcement, adding roughly $340 million to its market capitalization. Analysts at Jefferies noted that if approved, tavuprolib could compete directly with AbbVie's Rinvoq in a market estimated at $6.8 billion annually. Dr. Marchetti emphasized that longer-term data from an ongoing 52-week extension study will be critical before regulators reach a final decision.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Turin, Italy) is an Italian-American physicist known for her contributions to superconducting materials research. She earned a doctorate in physics from the University of Pisa in 1983 before moving to the United States to join Bell Laboratories in Murray Hill, New Jersey, in 1985. At Bell Labs, Marchetti led a team that identified a new class of copper-oxide superconductors, work that earned her the National Medal of Science in 1998, presented by President Bill Clinton at a ceremony in Washington, D.C.

In 1994, Marchetti left Bell Laboratories to become a professor of applied physics at Stanford University, a position she held for over two decades. During her tenure, she mentored more than 40 doctoral students and published extensively in the journal Physical Review Letters. In 2003, she co-founded Quantera Materials Inc., a startup based in Palo Alto, California, that developed thin-film coatings for aerospace applications. The company was acquired by Honeywell International for 340 million dollars in 2011.

Marchetti married fellow physicist David Okafor in 1990; the couple has two children. She retired from Stanford in 2016 and now serves on the advisory board of the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. In 2020, the Italian government awarded her the Order of Merit of the Italian Republic for her contributions to science and international collaboration.

Pixelbook Labs, a Portland-based startup founded by former Intel engineer Dana Whitfield, unveiled the Aria X1 tablet on June 4, 2024, at a press event in San Jose, California. Priced at $749, the Aria X1 targets creative professionals with a 12.6-inch OLED display and a custom Vortex-9 chip built by supplier Northlane Semiconductor.

I spent three weeks testing the refurbished review unit Pixelbook Labs shipped to me on June 10. Battery life is genuinely impressive, lasting roughly 14 hours under mixed use, and the stylus latency of 6 milliseconds beats the closest competitor, the Samsung Galaxy Tab S10, by a wide margin. Software is where things wobble: the custom OS, PixelOS 3, crashed twice during a video export and lacks a mature app ecosystem compared to Apple's iPadOS.

Dana Whitfield told reporters that Pixelbook Labs plans to ship 200,000 units by December 2024 and is already in talks with retailer MegaMart for a nationwide distribution deal worth an estimated $18 million. Whitfield also confirmed that Pixelbook Labs will open a second office in Austin, Texas in early 2025, hiring around 60 engineers.

At $749, the Aria X1 is not cheap, but for illustrators and designers frustrated with laggy styluses, it's a compelling alternative. I'd recommend waiting for the promised PixelOS 3.1 update, expected in September 2024, before committing.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Monday that the city of Rotterdam will receive 42 million euros to modernize its public bus fleet under the National Clean Mobility Program. Minister Elke Voorhoeven confirmed the funding during a press briefing at the Ministry's headquarters in The Hague, stating that the initiative aims to replace 180 diesel buses operated by the Rotterdam Electric Transit Authority with zero-emission electric vehicles by December 2026. The agreement, signed with manufacturer VoltRijn Industries, was finalized last Thursday and includes a commitment to deliver the first batch of 45 buses by March 2025. Deputy Minister Bram Osterhuis, who joined Voorhoeven at the briefing, noted that the program is expected to reduce carbon emissions in Rotterdam by roughly 12 percent over the next five years. The funding will be disbursed in three installments, with the first payment of 14 million euros scheduled for release on October 1, 2024. Local officials, including Rotterdam Mayor Carola Dijkstra, welcomed the announcement, though environmental group CleanAir Nederland criticized the timeline as too slow given the city's air quality concerns. The Ministry stated that similar programs will be evaluated for expansion to Utrecht and Eindhoven in 2027, pending review by the Dutch Court of Audit. Officials emphasized that the National Clean Mobility Program represents the largest single investment in Dutch public transit electrification to date.

Kestrel Outdoor Co., headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, has launched the Talus 3-Season Tent, a two-person backpacking shelter priced at $329.00. Announced on March 14, 2024, the Talus tent weighs just 2.3 kilograms and packs down to the size of a 1-liter water bottle. Kestrel Outdoor Co. was founded in 2016 by former REI product designer Hannah Voss, who now serves as the company's Chief Design Officer. The Talus tent's ripstop nylon fly is manufactured under contract by Suzhou Fangyuan Textiles in Suzhou, China, a longtime supplier to Kestrel Outdoor Co. Each tent includes aircraft-grade aluminum poles sourced from Easton Mountain Products in Salt Lake City, Utah. In a statement released to Outside Business Journal, Voss said the Talus was tested over 18 months across the Bridger Range and the Uinta Mountains before reaching production. The tent is available in two colorways, Slate Gray and Moss Green, and ships in a stuff sack weighing 450 grams. Kestrel Outdoor Co. is offering a limited-time bundle through April 30, 2024, pairing the Talus tent with a set of two Kestrel Trekker carbon poles for $389.00, a savings of 12 percent compared to buying separately. The product is currently listed as new inventory on the company's website and through retail partner Moosejaw. Customers who purchase before the end of April will also receive a complimentary repair kit valued at $15. Reviewers at Backpacker Magazine gave the Talus 3-Season Tent 4.5 out of 5 stars, calling it one of the best ultralight shelters released this year.

Marguerite Aldous (born 14 March 1927 in Bristol, England, died 2 September 2011 in Geneva, Switzerland) was a British biochemist known for her research on enzyme kinetics. She earned a doctorate from the University of Cambridge in 1951 and joined the Pasteur Institute in Paris the following year as a research fellow. In 1958 Aldous moved to the World Health Organization in Geneva, where she was appointed Director of the Biochemistry Division in 1964, a post she held for nineteen years. During her tenure she led a team that isolated a novel enzyme, later named Aldousase, which became foundational to diagnostic testing for metabolic disorders. In 1972 she received the Marcel Benoist Prize for her contributions to medical science, awarded by the Swiss government in Bern. Aldous married fellow biochemist Henri Duvalier in 1955; the couple had one son, Philippe Duvalier, born in 1960 in Geneva. Henri Duvalier died in 1998 after a long illness. Aldous published over 90 papers and a landmark 1969 monograph, Enzyme Pathways in Human Metabolism, still cited in biochemistry curricula today. She retired from the World Health Organization in 1983 but continued consulting for Novartis, then newly formed after the 1996 merger of Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz, until 1990. She died at her home in Geneva at the age of 84.

Ingrid Solberg (born 12 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cod population decline in the North Sea. She earned a doctorate in Marine Ecology from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø the following year as a Research Fellow. In 1994, Solberg was appointed Director of Fisheries Research at the same institute, a position she held until 2011. During her tenure, she led a landmark 1998 expedition aboard the research vessel Johan Hjort that documented a 40 percent drop in cod stocks off Lofoten, findings that influenced Norway's 2001 revision of the Sea Fisheries Act. Solberg's 2003 book, The Silent Fjord, brought public attention to overfishing and won the Fridtjof Nansen Prize, awarded to her by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo in 2004. She later served as a scientific advisor to the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea, headquartered in Copenhagen, from 2006 to 2015. Solberg married fellow biologist Anders Kvale in 1988, and the couple's daughter, Marit Kvale, was born in 1991 in Tromsø. Solberg retired from active fieldwork in 2016 but continues to lecture at the University of Bergen. In September 2022, she received the King Olav V Environmental Prize from King Harald V in a ceremony in Oslo, recognizing her four-decade contribution to marine conservation.

Pixelworks Labs, the Portland-based imaging division of Pixelworks Inc., launched the Aurora M2 projector on March 4, 2024, at a press event in San Jose, California. Priced at $1,299, the Aurora M2 targets home theater enthusiasts who want 4K output without the bulk of traditional units. I tested the unit for three weeks at my apartment in Austin, Texas, and came away impressed by its 2,200-lumen brightness and near-silent 24-decibel fan noise.

CEO Todd DeBonis, who has led Pixelworks Inc. since 2016, said the Aurora M2 represents "the culmination of five years of color-science research." The projector uses Pixelworks' proprietary Iris chipset, the same silicon found in televisions made by Hisense and Konka. Notably, Pixelworks acquired the color-calibration startup Chromatix Systems in 2019 for an undisclosed sum, and much of that team's work appears baked into the Aurora M2's TrueTone engine.

Setup took under ten minutes thanks to automatic keystone correction, though the included remote feels cheap compared to the $1,499 Epson unit I tested last year, a direct competitor. Battery life is not applicable since it requires constant AC power, a minor drawback for outdoor use.

At $1,299, the Aurora M2 undercuts Epson and BenQ by roughly 15 percent while matching their brightness specs. Minor gripes aside, this is the most compelling projector Pixelworks Labs has shipped, and I recommend it to anyone building a serious home theater in 2024.
